Sports.title: Enzo Maresca wants Chelsea star to replace Rodri as Barcelona move advances
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca wants Chelsea star to replace Rodri as Barcelona move advances

Barcelona have seen an opening bid for Manchester City midfielder Rodi turned down on Friday - but the La Liga giants are expected to return as they close in on the World Cup winner

View 3 Images Barcelona have launched an opening offer for Man City midfielder Rodri

Enzo Maresca has earmarked Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez as his top option to replace Rodri this summer.

‌



Barcelona have seen an opening offer of £38.5million rejected out of hand by City, who want closer to £60m. However, with just one year remaining on his contract and coming off a serious knee injury, City are open to selling at the right price.

‌



And Maresca, who is going into his first season as Pep Guardiola ’s replacement, sees Fernandez as the perfect replacement for the World Cup Golden Ball winner.

‌



The Italian worked with Fernandez during his time as Chelsea boss and according to the Independent, City are already exploring a possible move for the Argentinian.

Inside Bruno Guimaraes' dream Arsenal transfer six years in making for Mikel Arteta READ MORE :

Fernandez is yet to report for Chelsea this summer after playing a huge role in Argentina’s rollercoaster ride to the World Cup final. The 25-year-old scored crucial goals in the knockout stages, including a screamer in the dramatic comeback against England in the semis.

However, he arguably cost his nation the chance of lifting a fourth world title after he inexplicably picked up two yellow cards in a matter of minutes.

‌



Chelsea paid £106m for the midfielder in 2023 and would want to make a profit on that, if they were to entertain an exit this summer.

Fernandez was sanctioned earlier this year after his desire to leave the London club was made public. Ex-boss Liam Rosenior was also forced to strip him of the vice captaincy before he was sacked for a disastrous run of results.

View 3 Images Chelsea want a reported £120m for Enzo Fernandez (Image: Visionhaus/Getty Images)

‌



New Blues boss Xabi Alonso hasn’t been able to train with the talismanic midfielder during his short tenure, but made it clear he wants him to remain at the club.

Speaking in July, Alonso said: "Yes we have spoken. But as you can imagine what we have spoken remains private,” and then when pressed if he wanted Fernandez to stay, he replied “yes”.

City have already smashed their own transfer record this summer, signing Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for a whopping £116m. But with the exit of Bernardo Silva and the expected one of Rodri, more cover is required before the Premier League campaign begins.

‌



They have also been heavily linked with Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille, who shone at the World Cup with Morocco, but his £86m valuation has led talks to an impasse.

View 3 Images Enzo Maresca worked with Fernandez during his time as Chelsea boss

Speaking after City’s most recent pre-season friendly, Maresca admitted the club still had work to do in order to replace a number of senior players.

‌



“Fortunately this is a squad that doesn’t need to do many things,” he told media at a press conference ahead of Wednesday’s clash with K-League All Stars.

“At the same time, we already know the squad lost some important players with experience with Bernardo, John [Stones], Nathan [Ake]…different players. For sure, there are things we need to do.

He added: “The reason I said there are things to do is because the transfer window is open and when it is open, anything can happen. It is August and then from September, when it’s closed, it is completely different.”

Sports.title: Man Utd legends called out by former team-mate as Roy Keane in firing line
Sports.content:
Man Utd legends called out by former team-mate as Roy Keane in firing line

Roy Keane and several other Manchester United legends have been called out by a fellow Red Devils hero

View 3 Images Javier Hernandez has called out his former team-mates for criticising Michael Carrick

Roy Keane, Gary Neville and Paul Scholes have been called out by their former Manchester United team-mate Javier Hernandez for comments about Michael Carrick. Carrick did a remarkable job at the helm after being appointed as United’s interim head coach back in January.

‌



He managed to secure a third place Premier League finish and qualification to the Champions League, which was largely unthinkable under his predecessor Ruben Amorim earlier in the season. That has since seen the 45-year-old be appointed as the club’s permanent head coach ahead of the 2026/27 campaign.

‌



Yet, while many United fans and, evidently, the club have been pleased with Carrick’s tenure up to now, the former Red Devils midfielder has faced considerable criticism from the same people he shared a dressing room with during his 12-year stint as a player at Old Trafford.

‌



Roy Keane seemingly holds some bitterness towards Carrick, having made personal jibes, while Paul Scholes took to social media to have a dig at his former midfield partner following a loss to Newcastle. Gary Neville also cast doubt over Carrick's credentials for the role.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd finally announce sixth summer transfer as statement confirms next steps READ MORE :

Recently appearing on Rio Ferdinand Presents, Hernandez was asked for his thoughts about Carrick being at the helm and replied: "I love it, I love it.” Ferdinand then pointed out that several of the pair's former team-mates had been far less complimentary about Carrick.

‌



"I don’t know why. I really don’t know why. There’s a fine line between criticising someone’s job, because you have to, and then your own opinions," replied Hernandez.

"I’m very surprised, mostly because you know Carrick more than I do. You spent so much time with him, not only as a teammate at the club but also with the national team. Carrick was always a man who never had a problem with anyone.

View 3 Images Roy Keane has made some harsh comments about Carrick (Image: ITV)

‌



"The most civilised, calm person. So I don’t understand. How are you going to criticise a manager who is giving you results?

"He put your team back into the Champions League, so he deserves the consequence of that: stay, try to bring him players and give him the project. If it doesn’t work, it doesn’t work. But he took the team from low and put the team back into the Champions League."

Hernandez also spoke openly about his departure from United in 2015, admitting he felt the club had changed following the exits of Sir Alex Ferguson and David Gill in 2013.

‌



View 3 Images Michael Carrick has transformed Manchester United (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

He said: "It was very hard. Because if you gave me the chance to stay at United for most of my career, I would have taken it. The team that I played the most games for, even more than my hometown team in Mexico, is United.

"I would have taken a bullet for that team. It’s my team, Manchester United. But things weren’t the same. It’s not that I left the club that I was with; I left a different environment. It wasn’t the same club.

Article continues below

"With the departure, obviously, of Sir Alex Ferguson, but also David Gill and all that family structure. When I say family, it doesn’t mean that it was all nice, but there were values.

"I was very sad. Don’t get me wrong. I would have retired at United and I would take a bullet for that team. But it wasn’t the same team as the team that embraced me and gave me my first opportunity."

Sports.title: Arsenal star's gesture to Bruno Guimaraes ahead of £75m transfer comes to light
Sports.content:
Arsenal star's gesture to Bruno Guimaraes ahead of £75m transfer comes to light

Arsenal are preparing to confirm the £75m signing of Bruno Guimaraes after the soon-to-be former Newcastle captain completed his medical - and his shirt number seemingly been leaked

View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes will join Arsenal for £75million (Image: Mark Leech/Offside/Offside via Getty Images)

Bruno Guimaraes is set to wear the No.39 shirt for Arsenal after academy star Louie Copley moved to a new number. Arsenal are preparing to confirm Guimaraes' arrival from Newcastle after the two clubs agreed a fixed fee of £75million to end the transfer saga.

‌



The 28-year-old said his goodbyes at Newcastle's training camp in Spain before completing his medical with Arsenal and signing a four-year contract. His signing still hasn't been announced, although the Gunners have dropped a clear hint on their website.

‌



Copley, who wore the No. 39 shirt in each of Arsenal's first two pre-season friendlies as well as in training sessions, has had his squad number changed to 38. It's a telltale sign that Guimaraes is now a Gunner and has taken his favourite number.

‌



The midfielder has worn 39 throughout his club career, including for former clubs Lyon and Athletico Paranaense. Guimaraes likes to wear the number because his dad's taxi cab in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil was #039.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Inside Bruno Guimaraes' dream Arsenal transfer six years in making for Mikel Arteta READ MORE :

Tottenham respond as Arsenal consider shock transfer for Spurs skipper Cristian Romero READ MORE :

Whether the decision was Copley's is unknown, although he did wear No.38 when captaining Arsenal's under-21 side last season. Unfortunately for Copley, who's just 19 and highly regarded at London Colney, he suffered an injury just minutes after coming on as a half-time substitute during the Gunners' 3-1 loss against Real Betis in a friendly on Wednesday.

‌



Mikel Arteta said post-match: "It doesn't look good, the mechanism is not too positive, the symptoms that he already has either. Let's hope that tomorrow [Thursday] the news is better than we hope."

Guimaraes will become Arsenal's most expensive signing of the summer, with the Gunners having also brought in Christos Tzolis for £34m and Illan Meslier on a free transfer. The Brazilian is expected to partner Declan Rice in midfield once the season gets going.

Who should Arsenal sign next? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Louie Copley's number has been changed on the Arsenal website

By leaving Newcastle, Guimaraes becomes the third key player to depart St James' Park this summer as well as manager Eddie Howe. New Magpies boss Matthias Jaissle said: "I met him quickly, but the decision was already made. It was a nice conversation.

"He's a fantastic player and a great human being. It's tough but for him now it's the next challenge and we need to deal with it at a later stage. We trust the players who are here already, but we will also see some changes."

Sports.title: Terror plot to 'storm World Cup game with bombs and kill Lionel Messi' uncovered
Sports.content:
Terror plot to 'storm World Cup game with bombs and kill Lionel Messi' uncovered

FBI and IPCC logs show Lionel Messi received the most threats during the World Cup, including a disturbing incident where a man claimed he would carry guns and bombs to a game

View 2 Images Messi received the most threats during the World Cup (Image: DiaEsportivo/Action Plus/Shutterstock)

Terrorists planned to attack Lionel Messi by storming a World Cup match with guns and bombs, a police report states.

‌



A catalogue of threats were made during the tournament, held in the US, including from a man who was arrested trying to get into a lift with Cristiano Ronaldo.

‌



Reports from the International Police Cooperation Center (IPCC) and FBI also show the referee of the Argentina-Egypt match, Francois Letezier, was targeted with more than 6,000 threats on his personal WhatsApp - and his family back in France received police protection. The security reports have been revealed by Spanish newspaper Informacion.es.

‌



The reports note how one man wrote on X ahead of the Argentina clash with Egypt on July 7: "I'm going to walk into the Atlanta stadium and blow up Messi with four bombs stuck in my body."

View 2 Images There were many reports of Cristiano Ronaldo being harassed (Image: AP Photo/Tony Gutierrez)

Aldi and Lidl could soon be stopped from blocking rival supermarkets opening shops READ MORE :

The most concrete threat against Messi arose when a man called Dallas airport and announced that he and two other individuals were heading to the city's stadium with "homemade bombs and an AR-15".

‌



In his message, he stated that they intended to attack "police officers and players from both teams" but the alleged terrorist made "special mention of Lionel Messi".

Several explosives specialists, canine handlers and their K-9 agents searched the Atlanta stadium after another man called police during the game and announced he had left "three bombs" in litter bins in the stadium.

According to the dossier, Messi received the most threats while Ronaldo was the most harassed while during the competition.

‌



On June 14, a FIFA employee reported "a suspicious man" who was asking for "details" about Ronaldo's accommodation at his hotel. Houston police identified and arrested that man two days later when he was at the hotel where Ronaldo was staying with his national team.

Another man was arrested in Toronto for a very similar incident when Ronaldo was there. This time, the supporter tried to get into the elevator with the Portuguese star when he was arrested. He said he just wanted to take a selfie with CR7.

Other incidents with Ronaldo occurred in Miami, when a man tried to gain access to him, and during the Portugal-Croatia match, when a man dressed in a Ronaldo shirt jumped onto the field.

Article continues below

Another of the many players singled out with threats was Kylian Mbappé, who had an ongoing argument with Paraguay's goalkeeper during the clash with France.

The police report said the Real Madrid player was insulted with "xenophobic" abuse online, while a doll with Mbappé's image "was burned and broadcast" on social networks in Paraguay on July 5 and 6.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino state of play as 211 nations decide desperate FIFA president's fate
Sports.content:
'Bribery', a boycott and a grovelling apology. Just an ordinary week in the life of Gianni Infantino.

The FIFA president may have backed down on his controversial plan to sell off the World Cup, but he remains in his position. After all, Infantino was in charge of 'the greatest World Cup of all time' and 'the greatest human, social and cultural event that mankind has ever witnessed and seen'.

According to him, anyway. Still, UEFA are planning to boycott FIFA competitions after its 55 members unanimously voted to do so, firmly opposing Infantino's plan that would've seen private investors buy the World Cup and other tournaments.

Outside of Europe, though, it's a different story. The Confederation of African Football (CAF) gave its backing to Infantino on Thursday - a rare boost to the under-fire Swiss chief.

‌



And CAF isn't alone in its support. However, it'll be the 211 individual nations who'll vote to decide Infantino's future if or when he goes up for re-election in March 2027, not the federations.

Let's breakdown who's for backing and who's for sacking Infantino.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Fight to oust shameless Gianni Infantino is just starting - UEFA must not let up READ MORE :

UEFA standing firm (55 votes)

Starting with Infantino's most powerful opposition, the European football governing body isn't letting up on their stance. There've been tensions between the two organisations for years, with UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin notably not attending last month's World Cup final, despite a European nation (Spain) being involved.

‌



On Thursday, UEFA announced that its boycott still stands in a strong-worded statement. And, as of now, all 55 nations are unlikely to vote for Infantino regardless of their previous support.

"UEFA's associations were very clear about the conditions attached to the non-participation in FIFA competitions," the statement read. "First, the proposals to sell off the major competitions had to be withdrawn, and secondly, assurances have to be made that such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again.

"These conditions have not been met. In addition, UEFA made it abundantly clear in its statement on Saturday that it has lost confidence in Gianni Infantino's presidency. That position holds.

"Yesterday's [Wednesday] announcement that some people employed by the FIFA President (and whose careers depend on his favour) agree with him changes nothing."

‌



England's Football Association has already withdrawn its support for Infantino's re-election. It joined the FAs of Wales, Serbia, Sweden, Finland and Norway in publicly going against him.

Should Gianni Infantino be allowed to continue? Have your say in the comments section.

View 5 Images The relationship between Aleksander Ceferin and Gianni Infantino is strained (Image: Nicolò Campo/LightRocket via Getty Images)

Question marks over Asia (46 votes)

With 46 associations, the Asian Football Confedeation boasts the third-largest contingent of countries within FIFA. It joined UEFA in criticising Infantino's plan, having previously been in support of the 56-year-old and pledging to vote for him next year.

‌



However, AFC President Salman bin Ibrahim al-Khalifa wrote in a letter to its members: "The AFC notes with great concern and disappointment that it was not consulted by FIFA at any level prior to the public announcement of this proposal, and nor has it received any detailed governance, financial or legal analysis of the proposal and its potential repercussions, which is totally unacceptable.

"Furthermore, the AFC is deeply concerned that FIFA's unilateral actions appear to undermine the very foundations of continental football, which are based on solidarity, cooperation and transparency. Moreover, such an initiative will not succeed without the support of all the confederations, which is not the case now."

Now that the plan has been scrapped, though, could Infantino rekindle his support from Asia? The Jordan FA certainly won't be voting for him.

Its president, Prince Ali bin Al Hussein, accused FIFA of 'bribery' this week before belatedly receiving funds that should've been available eight months ago. However, Prince AIi and Jordan's stance on Infantino remains, saying: "While this is a good development for our players, it does not change the serious concerns we in the football world have regarding the FIFA leadership, nor does it change what our FAs have been subjected to in the past.

‌



"It is symptomatic of those exact difficulties that we all face, and that are usually linked to the FIFA presidential elections. And it does not change my clear position concerning the leadership of FIFA: my FA and I will not endorse president Infantino, nor will we vote for him."

View 5 Images Prince Ali bin Hussein of Jordan has vowed not to vote for Gianni Infantino (Image: David Ramos - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

CONCACAF divided (35 votes)

Within CONCACAF - the confederation which represents North America, Central America and the Caribbean - there's already division. CONCACAF declared a loss of confidence in Infantino last week by saying that it was 'deeply concerned by the lack of due process' regarding the sell-off plan, calling for a 'comprehensive reckoning' over FIFA's leadership.

However, 2026 World Cup co-hosts Mexico appear to have broken rank and has thrown its support behind Infantino. In a statement, the Mexican Football Federation (FMF) declared: "The Mexican Football Federation is convinced that football is its fundamental value and that its best defense lies in institutional integrity and respect for the governance and processes that safeguard it," the FMF said.

‌



"Therefore, the FMF will not recognise or approve any process convened outside of this institutional framework, and it embraces the call issued by President Infantino on August 5, 2026, to collectively continue developing football for the benefit of its 211 member associations.

"The FMF supports President Infantino's leadership in continuing to promote the development of football through institutional strengthening."

Prior to Infantino's climbdown, it was reported that CONCACAF's 41 members were considering withdrawing their letters of support for his re-election. Could Mexico's stance be a catalyst for support?

Should Gianni Infantino resign from FIFA? Have your say after scathing UEFA attack READ MORE :

CAF back Infantino (54 votes)

It's important to remember that despite the widespread backlash, Infantino still has friends dotted around the world. Africa will be a key player in next year's election and he can seemingly count on a huge 54 votes from the continent.

‌



CAF president Patrice Motsepe stated on Thursday that the federation welcomed FIFA's apology and will back Infantino. "For us in Africa, adherence to governance, due process and transparency is crucial and non-negotiable," Motsepe added.

"We are committed to continue working together with FIFA, its Member Associations, other Football Confederations and stakeholders to safeguard and adhere to governance, due process and transparency."

Motsepe previously affirmed: "I personally support Gianni Infantino. He's not just a good friend, he's a loyal friend. He's loyal to Africa. I come from a background where when people have been loyal to you, you never stab them in the back."

View 5 Images Patrice Motsepe says that Gianni Infantino has the support of CAF (Image: Patrick T. Fallon/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Argentina take stance after CONMEBOL indecision (10 votes)

With 10 members, the confederation for South American football is the smallest by number, although it boasts some of the most prestigious nations in the sport. And in good news for Infantino, CONMEBOL released a statement on Thursday confirming that it won't back a vote to oust him - although it was hardly a glowing endorsement.

It read: "Football belongs to everyone. Its future can only be built on the basis of respect for institutional governance, sound governance and the democratic procedures that represent FIFA's 211 Member Associations.

"On 18 November 2026, the deadline for submitting candidacies for the FIFA Presidency will expire. Thereafter, the FIFA Congress will elect, through the votes of its 211 Member Associations, the person who will lead the organisation during the next term, including overseeing the organisation of the FIFA Centennial World Cup 2030.

"Accordingly, CONMEBOL will not support any action or procedure that disregards or departs from those institutional mechanisms. The CONMEBOL Council calls for preserving the unity of the football family, acting with institutional responsibility, strengthening dialogue and fully respecting the mechanisms of governance. Because, above all differences, football comes first."

‌



It's important to note that three CONMEBOL nations - Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay - are co-hosting the 2030 World Cup, staging one game each before the tournament moves to its primary hosts: Spain, Portugal and Morocco. Argentina have also offered Infantino their backing in a lengthy statement.

View 5 Images Gianni Infantino can count on support from Argentina (Image: Alex Pantling - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

"Of our highest consideration, on behalf of the Argentine Football Association (AFA), and its Executive Committee, we address you, dear President, and through your worthy intermediary the FIFA board, to express our support for the management carried out during the last 10 years, which had as its main axes the development of football throughout the world and institutional solidity based on a clear governance model, stable and transparent," it began.

"In this sense, in relation to the recent events that are public knowledge, we must recognise the decision of the Administration to withdraw a project that generated, within the football family and from its inception, many more uncertainties than certainties.

‌



"That is why it is worth highlighting the acceptance of the errors made in this process and the apology expressed in the heartfelt message displayed to the 211 member associations of FIFA. Prioritising governance standards is a fundamental pillar for strengthening good relations between FIFA, its member associations and the confederations.

"In the same way, and as we have already expressed, you are leading a management that led to a profound transformation of FIFA, which opened the doors of the organisation to all member associations and confederations, so that with a frank and direct dialogue, we can, together, continue to promote football at all levels and disciplines.

"From our point of view, this transformation was based on a model of transparent governance, respect for statutory structures and the monitoring of democratic procedures, essential principles for the football family to be united, firm and working to continue generating improvements in sports and institutions, which have an impact on a better quality of life for millions of human beings who practice our beloved sport.

"Accordingly, with the upcoming FIFA Congress approaching, the Association that I proudly preside over firmly believes and reaffirms that the way forward is to continue to work under your leadership, so that we can continue to develop better and even more inclusive football."

‌



Oceania set for talks (11 votes)

The Oceania Football Confederation (OFC) will hold talks to decide its position on Wednesday, August 12. As revealed by GB News, the meeting will involve the 11 members who came up the OFC - New Zealand, American Samoa, the Cook Islands, Fiji, New Caledonia, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tahiti, Tonga and Vanuatu.

New Zealand Football boss Andrew Pragnell called for unity among the OFC earlier this week. "There's obviously more power in numbers .... Certainly it helps when a confederation acts in unison," Pragnell told Reuters after praising FIFA for its commercial efforts while reiterating that 'governance is governance'.

"You've seen in some confederations, even in the last week, members go different ways from other members. At the end of the day, the independence of each member association is respected as well."

Mirror Football's verdict

Gianni Infantino is going nowhere - at least for now. While countries and federations consider their positions, UEFA still have another card to play in what it believes is the fight to save football: a vote of no confidence.

‌



That can be triggered via an extraordinary congress at any time, potentially ousting Infantino before his re-election bid.

And, of course, there's the nuclear outcome: UEFA delivering on their promise to boycott FIFA tournaments. Should that happen, it's unfathomable that Infantino can continue, even until next year's elections.

A more realistic outcome would be an alternative candidate emerging in the coming months.

Paris Saint-Germain's Nasser al-Khelaifi, who's also chairman of the association of European Football Clubs, could be a popular choice given his friendships in the game, while the aforementioned Prince Ali has stood for FIFA president before.

‌



However, CONCACAF President Victor Montagliani is seen as the frontrunner. Montagliani has been praised for cleaning up the confederation following allegations of corruption and financial problems, and he helped bring the World Cup to his beloved Canada.

A FIFA President being liked by football fans? Imagine that...

Sports.title: Man Utd legend's blazing row with staff at local tip – 'I'm banned now'
Sports.content:
Man Utd legend's blazing row with staff at local tip – 'I'm banned now'

Former Manchester United midfielder Nicky Butt was left fuming when he was stopped from entering his local tip in his Range Rover

View 2 Images Nicky Butt has addressed the incident that led to him being banned from his local recycling centre

Nicky Butt has been kicked out of his local tip after a 'raging row' with workers. Butt, one of the Class of 92, blew his top when staff branded his Range Rover a commercial vehicle because the seats were folded flat. He dumped his 'smelling bags' anyway, prompting an employee to sprint after him.

‌



According to The Sun, Butt said: "There's this guy at the gate bit, and he flags me down and goes, 'Put your windows down I need to look in the back of your car'. I'm going, 'What for?'

‌



"I've got a lot of crap from the house, bit of cardboard... I missed the bin man last week, so I've got a few smelly bags.

‌



OPINION Man Utd dream attack as Marcus Rashford exits plus free agent striker and World Cup star join by Abbie Meehan

Michael Carrick's telling response after being told to sell eight players by Man Utd hero READ MORE :

"So I put the windows down, obviously my seats were down and apparently I'm not going in because it's a commercial van.

"So I'm raging, literally. I'm putting a bit of cardboard in the tip."

‌



Butt also claimed he was told he was 'sneaking' rubbish into the tip due to the blacked out windows on his Range Rover.

He added: "I thought, well, I'm there now, I'm gonna go for it. So I've got up the ramp, I see this bloke getting up...

"Trying to chase me up the hill, but he's got his walkie-talkie out.

‌

"So I've literally got up the top, throw all the bags out, and I'm going back down the hill, and he's going mad at me.

‌



"Anyway, I'm banned from the tip."

A spokesperson for Recycle for Greater Manchester has since spoken out and said: “We’re sorry to hear about Nicky’s experience, but would like to reassure him that he is still very welcome to use any of the 19 Recycle for Greater Manchester recycling centres across the region.”

Butt was a vital cog in the United machine throughout the 1990s, collecting six Premier League titles, three FA Cups and the Champions League before his switch to Newcastle in 2004.

‌



He remained at St James' Park for another six years, which included a loan spell at Birmingham City, before calling time on his playing career following a stint in China.

Since retiring, he has taken on various positions at United and owned a share in Salford City, where he served as CEO between 2022 and 2024.

Sports.title: Flintoff steps down as England Lions head coach
Sports.content:
Andrew Flintoff has stepped down as head coach of the England Lions.

Flintoff began in the role in September 2024, meaning he leaves just under two years in.

In June it was announced Flintoff would become head coach of Sydney Thunder in Australia's Big Bash League.

On the decision, Flintoff said: "Unfortunately I've made the decision to step away from my role with the Lions. Not only have I enjoyed my time having the opportunity to work with the best young cricketers in the country, but have taken great pride in seeing them develop.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Relive the top highlights from Andrew Flintoff's seven-game stint with Brisbane Heat in 2014/15.

"I'd like to thank the coaches and staff for all their passion, tireless work and support they give every day. In particular, Ed Barney who I've loved working with and was so lucky to have as a performance director, and obviously Rob (Key) for trusting me with one of the most important roles in English cricket.

"I can't wait to get started with the Thunder later in the year and see where coaching takes me."

Ed Barney, ECB men's performance director, said: "Fred has helped to transform the Lions environment into a programme that has had a major impact on young players. By creating an environment that both supports and pushes excellence at all times he has helped bring forward a new generation of young players.

"Coaches have also flourished alongside him, whether early in their coaching journey or with decades of experience, and he has consistently maximised the expertise around the group. We wish him the best in the next stage of his coaching career and look forward to a time he returns to the English game."

Mike Yardy will step in as head coach for the four-day Professional County Club Select XI match against Pakistan Men, which begins at Beckenham on Wednesday August 12.

Sports.title: White: I know where the Fury-AJ venue is - I did the deal!
Sports.content:
The long-awaited heavyweight showdown between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will take place "where the money is", says Dana White.

White, who founded the UFC and new promotion Zuffa Boxing, is a major figure in combat sports. He revealed that he knows where Fury vs Joshua will take place.

"We're the ones that have done all the deals for this fight. I did the deal for the venue, that's why I know where the venue is. I did the deal. We at TKO [the company which owns UFC, WWE and Zuffa Boxing] did the deal for television and we did everything," White told Sky Sports.

There has been much speculation that Fury vs Joshua could take place in the United States rather than Britain, with Eddie Hearn, Joshua's promoter, claiming: "I really feel strongly that this is something that should happen in the UK and we'll do all we can."

White told Sky Sports: "At the end of the day, here's the truth, you're going to go where the money is."

Heavyweight rivals Joshua and Fury have been circling one another for almost a decade and yet a fight between the pair has never come to fruition.

"It's just been such a [mess]. It's unbelievable what a [mess] this thing has been," White said.

"It goes to show why boxing has been so [messed] up for so long. Look at this. It's definitely not about the money. The Saudis are paying for this fight. So they're making [a lot] of money. And what I've noticed is in the boxing business since I've been in it for a very short period of time, six months, the promoters' egos are actually more important than the fights themselves and giving the fight fans the fights they want to see.

"It's all about ego with the promoters. It's fascinating. These guys are all really weak, some of the weakest people I've ever encountered in the fight game. It's fascinating."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Eddie Hearn claimed that Anthony Joshua feels a responsibility to UK fight fans that AJ vs Fury should happen in the UK.

Sky Sports has contacted Matchroom and Queensberry, the promoters of Joshua and Fury, for comment.

Fury was a guest at White's UFC event at the White House and the promoter has known both fighters from before he launched his own boxing business.

"I've talked about Anthony Joshua after he beat (Wladimir) Klitschko and I was like that's what boxing needs, good looking, charismatic, good speaking heavyweight champion. So I've always really liked Anthony Joshua," White said.

"There was a point in time where Tyson was stagnant and trying to get fights so he started talking [trash] about UFC fighters, trying to get a payday one way or another and that was around the time that I met him and I've always liked him.

"Tough as hell, when he was dropped by (Deontay) Wilder [and] he gets right back up like a zombie and finishes the fight. He's a fun guy to watch. He's one of the best ever."

Sports.title: Doyle: Thunder Call a big player in Ascot's Shergar Cup
Sports.content:
Our ambassador Hollie Doyle, who was the leading rider at the 2023 Shergar Cup, runs the rule over Saturday's international contest at Ascot - live on Sky Sports Racing.

Glamorous can have them singing in the Valleys

It's exciting for Welsh trainer Chris Mason to have a runner in this year's Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup and they'll be singing loud in his Monmouth village on Saturday night if All Ways Glamorous takes the opening Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Dash (1.35) at Ascot.

His five-year-old, who will be representing Team Europe, already has a course-and-distance win to his name after impressing off a five-pound lower rating two weeks ago and can give French rider Marie Velon a great experience.

Europe's Bolo Neighs looks poised to get his head in front soon after flashing home in the same race last time but has work to do to turn the tables, while Ryan Moore can be relied upon to get the best out of my old friend Spartan Arrow who has been working well enough to put points on the board for Great Britain and Ireland.

Shady has Moore to offer in Stayers

Shrimp Shady is a young horse going places and can give Great Britain and Ireland maximum points in the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Stayers (2.10).

Andrew Balding's four-year-old has landed big marathon handicaps at Chester and Newbury already this summer and looks made for this stiff two-mile trip with Ryan Moore set for another plum ride.

Europe, who haven't won the Shergar Cup since back-to-back triumphs in 2013 and 2014, are also well represented with the Ian Williams-trained Hermetic likely to build on his fourth at Newcastle under the classy Christophe Lemaire. This ex-French winner could be well treated off a mark of 81.

Castle in driving seat for Ferraris

It was good to see Richard and Peter Fahey come off the cold list at Southwell on Thursday, just in time for Castle Stuart's run in the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Challenge (2.45).

Hong Kong, who are competing as a team for the first time, have a live contender in this reliable four-year-old who has been unfortunate to bump into two Roger Varian improvers at York this summer. South African Luke Ferraris, a well-known name in China, can be relied upon to get the best out of him.

Ian Williams has the services of Irish champion Dylan Browne McMonagle on his likely favourite Night Breeze, a consistent sort who was a good third at Goodwood but needs a career best to win this, which could make him a shade vulnerable. Insanity took this two years ago for Rachel King and can go well again under Europe's Velon.

Thunder a big player for Hong Kong debutant

Thunder Call didn't appear to enjoy Newmarket's undulations last time but can get back to winning ways for the Hong Kong team in the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Sprint (3.20).

William Haggas' sprinter won in the style of a very nice horse at York before that and promises to be ideally suited to the stiff finish at Ascot, with British racing debutant Jerry Chau on board.

One to watch out for is Great Britain and Ireland's Cape Ashizuri who is unexposed enough to put a disappointing run in a big field last time behind him. John and Sean Quinn will be happy to have McMonagle in the plate.

Archers can hit the target for Ryan

Newmarket-based Italian trainer Marco Botti can put maximum points on the scoreboard for Great Britain and Ireland in the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Classic (3.55).

Archers Bay, another strong chance for Moore, has been bumping into the likes of Ancient Egypt and Heraldry since winning at Newmarket - form that stands out in what doesn't look the strongest renewal.

Team-mate Hoseki is on a roll after rattling up a hat-trick in a course-and-distance fillies' race under a light weight. I'm not sure how much improvement she has left off this five-pound higher mark, though. A more interesting proposition could be Jessie Harrington's Pierre Grosse who is still a maiden but brings solid form to the race in first-time cheekpieces.

Bullet to make a Point in Cup decider

The closing Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Mile (4.30) could determine where the trophy goes this year with Europe's Bullet Point the one I expect to capitalise.

Lemaire partners Haggas' gelding, who has the sheepskins on for the first time after not hitting top stride in two starts this year. He is only a pound higher than when he won a big handicap at York's Ebor Festival 12 months ago.

I also like Rest of the World's Ebt's Guard, a course-and-distance winner who has run well in big handicaps at Royal Ascot and Sandown and looks a big player for Indian ace Suraj Narredu, who won the competition with Team Asia last year.

Special memories of the Shergar Cup

The Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup has given me some of my most special days on a racecourse and I'm excited to watch the action unfold in front of what will once again be a big, enthusiastic crowd at Ascot.

I've been lucky enough to ride three winners in the competition including a double three years ago when I was presented with the Alistair Haggis Silver Saddle Trophy for the highest points scorer.

I was on the winning team in 2023 and 2018 and can tell you that lifting that cup is such a buzz. Being part of a team competition is something we don't often experience as jockeys so the rivalry out on the turf on Saturday will be intense.

Sports.title: Draper will play Cincinnati Open despite arm injury fears
Sports.content:
Jack Draper has been confirmed for next week's Cincinnati Open despite being left in a flood of tears following defeat at the National Bank Open in Montreal.

Draper's hopes of playing in the US Open had looked to be in doubt after his latest comeback attempt saw him break down in tears mid-match.

The 24-year-old was playing his first match since June in Canada having suffered a recurrence of the bone bruising that kept him out for almost seven months.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the first-round match at the Canadian Open between Draper and Terence Atmane

Draper looked in discomfort, with his serve badly affected against France's Terence Atmane. After being broken to trail 4-1 in the third set, Draper sat on his chair and sobbed, eventually losing 6-3 2-6 6-2.

"This is pretty emotional actually. He's been bent over and just literally erupting with emotion here. Very, very upsetting to see. It just happened at the change of ends, he leaned forward," former British No 1 Annabel Croft told viewers on Sky Sports.

Croft added: "He knows what's going on inside his body, and he knows the work he's done to try and get back on court."

The Brit has been given a wild card for the Masters 1000 event in Cincinnati beginning next week - live on Sky Sports Tennis, while the US Open - for which he would also need a wild card into the main draw - starts on August 30.

Mixed doubles at US Open

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the US Open mixed doubles match of Draper and Jessica Pegula vs Emma Raducanu and Carlos Alcaraz

Draper is due to play in the mixed doubles at Flushing Meadows the preceding week with Jessica Pegula, and the American admitted their participation is now in doubt.

Speaking to reporters in Canada, Pegula said: "I know that he's been really struggling a bit with some injuries and I saw today he had a really tough day with his match.

"We're supposed to play. Obviously I know he's not healthy, so we'll see how that goes."

Pegula and Draper reached the semi-finals last year, and she added: "I've always since then been a very big fan, and it's been fun to watch him. He's a really nice kid, so I enjoy playing with him.

"Hoping that he can just get healthy and we can see him back out there."

Draper's injury woes

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Draper says his focus is on a 'rebirth' after suffering the 'perfect storm' of injury issues in recent times

If Draper is unable to play in New York, it would be a fourth consecutive Grand Slam that he has missed through injury.

Draper's problems first surfaced after a second-round exit at Wimbledon last year, with the former US Open semi-finalist forced off the tour with a bone bruise in his left arm.

He tried to make a comeback at Flushing Meadows but pulled out ahead of his second-round match and did not play again until February.

After initial positive signs, including victory over Novak Djokovic in Indian Wells, a changed service motion to try to help his arm problem led to a knee injury that kept him out for another lengthy spell.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Indian Wells match between Draper and Novak Djokovic

Returning just ahead of Wimbledon in Eastbourne, Draper looked strong and reached the semi-finals only to announce on the eve of his home Grand Slam that his arm had flared up again and he would be unable to play.

Speaking to Sky Sports ahead of Montreal, Draper said: "It's important for people to recognise that the injury I have is very complex, it's very complicated, and everyone around me is doing everything we can to help this keep moving along.

"It really has been a perfect storm for me in a lot of ways. When I do get out of this storm, I'm going to be pushing on to hopefully get to where I want to be and beyond."

Sports.title: Mexico and Argentina line up behind Infantino to deepen football’s civil war
Sports.content:
Mexico’s football federation has broken ranks with the rest of Concacaf by publicly backing the beleaguered Gianni Infantino in a move that has deepened world football’s civil war.

Concacaf has called for a thorough review of Fifa’s governance in the light of the World Cup sell-off debacle, and is backing Uefa’s demands for meaningful change, although has yet to follow its European counterparts by threatening to boycott tournaments if they do not achieve their objectives.

In a statement issued on Thursday night, the FMF went some way towards explaining Concacaf’s reticence, as its second-biggest member after the US was unequivocal in its support for the Fifa president. In a Fifa statement released under Infantino’s name on Wednesday, the world governing body had called for its institutional practices to be respected, a coded way of condemning any leadership challenge before next March’s scheduled presidential election, which the FMF endorsed.

“The Mexican Football Federation is convinced that football is its fundamental value and that its best defence lies in institutional integrity and respect for the governance and processes that safeguard it,” the FMF said. “Therefore, the FMF will not recognise or approve any process convened outside of this institutional framework, and it embraces the call issued by president Infantino on 5 August 2026 to collectively continue developing football for the benefit of its 211 member associations.

“The FMF supports president Infantino’s leadership in continuing to promote the development of football through institutional strengthening.”

The Argentina Football Association (AFA) followed Mexico’s lead by backing Infantino in a gushing tribute and expressing support for his leadership over the past decade. Unlike Concacaf, South America’s Conmebol appears united behind Infantino, while in an intriguing subplot there is growing speculation that Mexico would like to switch confederations to join the latter.

“In relation to the recent events that are public knowledge, we must recognise the decision of the administration to withdraw a project that generated, within the football family and from its inception, many more uncertainties than certainties,” the AFA statement read.

“That is why it is worth highlighting the acceptance of the errors made in this process and the apology expressed in the heartfelt message displayed to the 211 member associations of Fifa. Prioritising governance standards is a fundamental pillar for strengthening good relations between Fifa, its member associations and the confederations.

“In the same way, and as we have already expressed, you are leading a management that led to a profound transformation of Fifa, which opened the doors of the organisation to all member associations and confederations, so that with a frank and direct dialogue, we can, together, continue to promote football at all levels and disciplines.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“This transformation was based on a model of transparent governance, respect for statutory structures and the monitoring of democratic procedures, essential principles for the football family to be united, firm and working to continue generating improvements in sports and institutions, which have an impact on a better quality of life for millions of human beings who practise our beloved sport.

“Accordingly, with the upcoming Fifa congress approaching, the association that we proudly preside over firmly believes and reaffirms that the way forward is to continue to work under your leadership, so that we can continue to develop better and even more inclusive football.”

Earlier on Thursday, the Confederation of African Football had reaffirmed its support for Infantino, providing him with further allies as he fights to extend his 10-year reign.

Sports.title: Norway’s Klaveness tells Fifa president Infantino to resign: ‘There is no trust now’
Sports.content:
The Norwegian FA will ask Gianni Infantino to resign with immediate effect after his doomed attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Norway is the first federation to call directly for the Fifa president to step down after a series of controversies that came to a head with the crisis engulfing his Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme.

The decision was made at a meeting of the Norwegian Football Federation board (NFF) on Thursday night. Norway has consistently taken a lead in efforts to scrutinise Fifa’s governance and recent events have taken any faith in its leadership beyond the point of no return.

“We decided that there is no trust in Infantino now,” the NFF president, Lise Klaveness, told the Guardian. “We have been worried consistently and there has been one more step in a worrying direction every year, every part of the year. The trust is now gone for us, there is no way back for Infantino.

“We’re left in a very polarised cooperation globally and, I would say, chaos. So we will ask him to resign immediately so that the global football community can look ahead and cooperate going into the future.”

The NFF is expected to formally write a letter requesting Infantino’s resignation in the coming week. Norway was among a handful of countries not to back his re-election as president next March, although several European federations have withdrawn their endorsement in the past week.

“We understand that we’re one country, but it’s our position,” Klaveness said. “It’s just one step further for us. We did not vote for him in 2023 but we hoped we would support him, he was elected and the reason why we were so clear in our statements was to really give the signal that we wanted him to implement the good reforms he was part of. But he didn’t, and now we will ask him to resign.”

The NFF agreed to demand a full review into the package of reforms passed upon Infantino’s ascent to the presidency in 2016, which were intended to extricate Fifa from the corruption crisis that had previously dogged the governing body. Klaveness said the investigation should ask “what was implemented, what was not, what should have been implemented and what we should also implement to make this a functioning organisation”.

Norway will also formalise a fresh complaint to Fifa’s ethics committee on three fronts, taking in the FFE scandal, the award of Fifa’s peace prize to Donald Trump and the Folarin Balogun affair at the World Cup. It will attempt to bring a number of major European federations on board for its submission in an effort to further increase the pressure on Infantino.

“We want the ethics committee to show their work transparently because this is a very big part of the issue,” Klaveness said. “There are all kinds of control mechanisms in place but they are not really holding the council and president accountable.”

View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino leaves after attending the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations match between Malawi and Zambia in Rabat. Photograph: AP

In June, the NFF wrote to the ethics committee supporting a complaint by the advocacy group FairSquare, which centred on alleged breaches of political neutrality by Infantino. It will now make a new submission that asks for the three situations to be considered individually. “We will join them in one letter but they are very different cases and we want the ethical committee to treat them separately,” Klaveness said.

The NFF is understood to have particular concerns that the timing of Infantino’s FFE offer, which promised federations significant financial gains if accepted, may constitute an abuse of position at this proximity to a presidential election. It has also been observed that the FFE scheme, had it been passed, would have locked in commitments extending well beyond Infantino’s term.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to The Recap The best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s action Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

As with its call for Infantino to step down, Norway is the first federation to adopt a public stance regarding the peace prize or the Balogun case. Fifa’s decision to suspend the USA striker’s red card during the World Cup, meaning he was free to face Belgium in the last 16, came after Trump had called Infantino to discuss the ban.

Uefa’s federations have stood together in backing a potential boycott of Fifa competitions, a stance Uefa reasserted on Thursday despite Infantino’s shelving of FFE. Klaveness said the move is not merely symbolic and is intended to bring swift results.

“There’s no point in Uefa standing in a war position for half a year,” she said. “That would not be good at all. Now it’s crucial that we do it because global football cooperation is at stake. It’s very good to see we have strong leadership in Uefa that knows now is crunch time for this case. We cannot sell out this core of football.”

The first competition in line for a boycott would be the Under-20 Women’s World Cup, which is due to start in Poland on 5 September, but Klaveness expects the continued turmoil to have been resolved by then.

“I hope and think it will not come to that,” she said. “A lot of water will go under the bridge before that. But this is why we ask Infantino to resign. It’s so unstable now that it’s a matter of time. He cannot recover this and we cannot put the sport on the spot. The biggest priority is to be together with Uefa and have this strong position.”

Klaveness and the NFF have held a consistent line in calling for scrutiny of Fifa’s operations since she assumed her position in March 2022. She has been vocal on human rights issues and governance standards within Fifa, criticising failings surrounding the Qatar World Cup and questioning the process that awarded Saudi Arabia the 2034 edition of the tournament.

Sports.title: England striker Ivan Toney charged with assault after Soho nightclub incident
Sports.content:
The England footballer Ivan Toney has been charged with assault after an incident at a nightclub in Soho in December last year.

Scotland Yard said the striker had been charged on 31 July with assault causing actual bodily harm. Toney, who plays for the Saudi Pro League club Al-Ahli, is due to appear at Westminster magistrates court on 24 September.

The Sun newspaper reported in December that Toney had been arrested after an alleged head-butt. It claimed a fan recognised the footballer and grabbed at him while seeking a photograph with him before the incident.

On Friday the Metropolitan police said the charges related to an incident on 6 December at a nightclub on Wardour Street in central London, reportedly the now-closed 100 Wardour Street.

A spokesperson for Toney said: “Ivan acknowledges the charge and although he is naturally shocked, he looks forward to being given the opportunity to clear his name in court.”

Toney was at the centre of one of the most curious transfers on deadline day in August 2024 when he completed a late move from Brentford to Al-Ahli worth a reported £40m. He has also played for Newcastle United and his home town club Northampton Town, as well as several others on loan as he looked to establish himself.

Seen as a late bloomer in football terms, he had made only two Premier League appearances before his 25th birthday, but went on to score 67 goals in 128 appearances over the next three seasons at the top level.

He has played 10 times for England, scoring once in a friendly match against Belgium in 2024, and was part of the 2026 World Cup squad, making appearances against Argentina in the semi-final and in the win over France as England finished third.

Sports.title: Boardroom struggle deepens gloom as West Ham prepare for life on the outside
Sports.content:
There have been 10 summers of West Ham’s London Stadium tenancy and a number of winters of discontent. As the Hammers kick off the new season on Saturday, a Carabao Cup first-round fixture with Portsmouth is a stark reminder of reduced circumstances, further confirmation of last season’s relegation from the Premier League. The summer has been as bleak as any of those winters, with a number of factors colliding to deepen the gloom of relegation.

Certain clubs, including West Ham back in 2011-12 when promotion was achieved at first time of asking under Sam Allardyce, have used the Championship to take a beat, to refresh and replenish. Can this be the case at West Ham 2026? The Hammers are short-odds favourites for promotion but behind the scenes it has been a summer of turbulence, particularly in the boardroom, where a power struggle is being fought.

Portsmouth will bring 9,000 supporters on Saturday but will David Sullivan be present? This week it was revealed the operators of London Stadium had recommended the former joint-chair (but still co-owner) stay away, because of the “potential for demonstrations and anti-social behaviour by some spectators”.

It is expected that Sullivan will turn up, despite a fans’ advisory board statement that his attendance would cause “offence and upset”. It has been suggested that he wants to enjoy the coming season as a fan and is happy to bide his time before any consideration of selling his 38.8% stake. Considering his personal circumstances, his attendance would be a brazenly unpopular act. On 25 May, when relegation was confirmed despite a home win over Leeds, Sullivan was forced to leave the stadium early for his own safety.

View image in fullscreen Daniel Kretinsky wants to increase his shares in West Ham to just under 50.1%. Photograph: David W Černý/Reuters

Sullivan continues to deny allegations of sexually exploitative and predatory behaviour towards women over several decades made by the BBC’s Panorama documentary in early June, though he stepped down from his role on the eve of the broadcast “to avoid disruption to the club while he addresses the matter privately”.

Even before those allegations became public, Sullivan was a lightning rod, lambasted for his stewardship of a club in vertiginous decline since winning the Europa Conference League in May 2023. The £100m fee received for Declan Rice that summer was frittered away. Fellow Prague hero Jarrod Bowen, the club captain, has pledged to stay on, tasked with leading the club back up.

Until his defenestration Sullivan had acted as the club’s de facto director of football, often to the frustration of those in the football department. His chief ally, Karren Brady, stepped down in April as storm clouds gathered, severing a working relationship that dated as far back as 1990.

Among the club’s support, 50,000 season tickets have been sold for the attempt at re-entry to the Premier League. The overriding desire among fans is for Sullivan to completely depart the scene. His announced departure had installed a modicum of optimism.

Potential new sheriffs are circling but the picture is complicated, any future direction opaque as a result. As Sullivan stepped down the expectation was that Daniel Kretinsky, the Czech billionaire owner of Royal Mail who has owned 27% of West Ham since 2021, would make his move. Instead, this week, he cut that share down to just under 25%, though this was part of a strategy.

Last weekend, the familiar face of Amanda Staveley entered the picture. In July 2024 she departed Newcastle, after her leading role in bringing in the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund, but now Staveley wants to return to football. Last September, she was linked with a takeover at Tottenham, and it is suggested she will use a similar source of funding to engineer her move for West Ham. Among Newcastle fans, with their club faltering this summer, Staveley’s energy is lamented. With her connections, some Hammers fan hope she could have a similar galvanising effect.

View image in fullscreen David Sullivan’s closet ally, Karren Brady, left the club in April. Photograph: PA Images/Alamy

The key is the 25% that belonged to the late David Gold, Sullivan’s former joint-chair. As Staveley loomed, Kretinsky appeared ready to take up his first refusal on purchasing that 25% from Vanessa Gold, David’s daughter and current co-chair. Adding that to his 27% would take him beyond 50.1%, leaving him liable for a formal takeover offer. But shifting 2% to a Czech ally, the entrepreneur Jakub Havrlant, now means he would be short of that obligation should he cut across Staveley’s ambitions by buying Gold’s stake. Sullivan’s shares also hold the balance of power and Staveley’s next move is keenly awaited.

While that plays out, what of football? The arrival of free agent, the former Brighton and Ajax defender, Joël Veltman, was the first addition of a summer where the sales of Mateus Fernandes to Tottenham and Crysencio Summerville to Al-Hilal fetched a collective £140m, commensurate to a year of Premier League TV money. Youth product Freddie Potts’ departure to Club Brugge for £10m disappointed some fans. Needs must if further players are to arrive. There is interest in Ireland’s World Cup playoff hero Troy Parrott, the striker at AZ Alkmaar, though attracting players to the Championship has its difficulties.

View image in fullscreen West Ham have cashed in on key players, such as Mateus Fernandes to Tottenham, to cushion their descent into the Championship. Photograph: Phil Walter/Getty Images

In the dugout remains Nuno Espírito Santo, who stayed when his departure had been expected. Nuno’s zen-like calm is required at a club where panic regularly sets in. The vacuum created by Sullivan’s situation, relegation and lack of transfer business heightens anxieties. A new season has arrived, with uninviting league fixtures against Burnley, Charlton, Watford and Wolves by 1 September. Karim Virani, previously a club employee who departed in 2020, more recently at Glasgow Rangers, has returned as interim chief executive. Attempts are being made to stitch West Ham into a semblance of unity.

This summer, the London Stadium played host to concerts from Take That and Metallica, and staged the Diamond League athletics meet in July, where Josh Kerr broke the world mile record. Thursday saw a bid confirmed to stage the 2029 World Athletics Championships, following an impasse between the club and the stadium owners. Further reminders that West Ham’s home will never be fully their own, 10 years after departing the Boleyn Ground.

Such were the terms Sullivan, Gold Sr and Brady agreed for a stadium that fans continue to resent, where Sullivan is unlikely to be made to feel welcome.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Vinícius Júnior and a fantasy world of transfers in the football lull
Sports.content:
THE CAPTIVE VOID OF NOBLE RAGE

“We were so close … At the end of the day, really, they made him an offer he couldn’t refuse … It shows where we’re trying to aim for the club … There has been a lot of stuff written in the papers that you have to take on the chin I’m afraid – they should be talking about how well the England cricket team are playing at the moment.” Words said not by Mikel Arteta about Arsenal missing out on Vinícius Júnior after the Brazilian megastar signed a new Real Madrid contract, but by Glenn Hoddle in 2002, as Tottenham missed out on signing … yes, Rivaldo. That last sentence was probably a dead giveaway. Tottenham’s solution to the Brazilian-shaped hole in their transfer ambitions was to sign Robbie Keane to his boyhood club. What might Arsenal do next? Eye up Cristian Romero, you say?

Arsenal’s unrequited chase for Vinícius brought to bear the fantasy world that fans reside in when the transfer window is open and no actual competitive football is being played. Just imagine what he might have done to defences in Our League. In that netherworld of reverie there are no wet Tuesday nights at Stoke, nobody gets knacked, nobody fails to settle, they just score a gazillion goals and outperform their xG. Imagine football heaven, it’s easy if you try.

There is a flip side. Transfer business, or lack thereof, can also lead to a summer of angst. See the social media disgrace wails of certain vocal fans at Liverpool and their exasperation that Virgil van Dijk, 73, is the sole senior Red Men centre-back. Perhaps the balm of signing Bradley Barcola will soothe, though that is not yet a DONE DEAL. Arsenal fans have already consoled themselves with the imminent addition of Bruno Guimarães; who needs Big Vin when the other Brazilian can supply passes to, er Gabriel Martinelli?

Each summer includes a deal that unlocks others. In a sign of the times, Madrid ponying up for a mega Vinícius deal rather than his doing one will likely shift tectonic plates. With him set to stay, Rodri whose winning of the 2024 Ballon d’Or caused an almighty strop from the Brazilian and his club, lest we forget, is now highly unlikely to head to the Bernabéu. With Kylian Mbappé already on silly money, and now Vinícius too, thus there is no room at the inn for the Spain captain. Instead, Manchester City’s main man and the Geopolitics World Cup’s very best player is said to want to join Barcelona, which would be a huge loss to his current club and Our League. Such is the transfer window, where it is far better to have loved and lost than never to have signed anyone at all.

LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE

It’s Friday night. It’s Littlewoods Cup time. Join Billy Munday for updates from Middlesbrough 0-0 Wrexham (1-0 on pens) from 8pm BST.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“We have been worried consistently and there has been one more step in [a] worrying direction every year, every part of the year. The trust is now gone for us, there is no way back for Infantino” – Norwegian Football Federation president Lise Klaveness calls on Gianni Infantino to do one, although the civil war engulfing Fifa has deepened with Mexico and Argentina backing him.

View image in fullscreen Lise Klaveness, having none of it. Photograph: Amanda Pedersen Giske/EPA
