Sports.title: Antonelli vs Russell: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Early in the season it seemed certain that whichever of the Mercedes drivers came out ahead would be crowned world champion. That remains likely, but the threat posed by rival teams has grown in recent races.

Little about Andrea Kimi Antonelli’s form in his rookie season indicated that 12 months later he would be beating his team mate quite as emphatically as he is. But heading into the summer break, Antonelli holds a valuable 59-point lead over the other Mercedes driver.

It’s a far cry from the situation around 12 months ago. At the end of the ‘European season’, Antonelli was 15-1 down against George Russell in qualifying. He ended the season still with less than half his team mate’s points tally.

But after a difficult mid-season, following a Mercedes upgrade which did not go as intended, Antonelli rebounded impressively with the end of the year in sight. He reached the podium twice over the final four rounds.

So while Russell’s season-opening victory in Australia looked like the shape of things to come, Antonelli shattered those illusions by winning the next five rounds in a row. He got the rub of the green at times – technical trouble hit Russell in qualifying at Shanghai and took him out while he led in Montreal – but he has also seemed fundamentally more at ease with Mercedes’ W17 than his team mate.

The unusually high rate of problems on Mercedes’ cars, and Russell’s particular problems with poor straight-line speed at Silverstone and Spa, have further complicated the picture. Antonelli’s car has not been immune, breaking down in Spain and breaking an aerodynamic component at Silverstone. Overall, Russell has probably had slightly worse luck, but not 59 points’ worth. Antonelli is leading this championship on merit, and Russell will have to dig deep in the second half of the season if he is going to avoid a painful defeat.

Sports.title: Featured Comment: How far is modern F1 like the ‘turbo era’? | Formula 1
Asian Le Mans Series to take place entirely in Europe following war in Middle East | Brief
Sports.content:
The Asian Le Mans Series has announced its 2026-27 season will take place entirely at European circuits.

Since 2021 the series has only raced at the Dubai Autodrome, Yas Marina in the United Arab Emirates and Malaysia’s Sepang International Circuit. Its upcoming championship will take place at Jerez in Spain, Paul Ricard in France and Autodromo do Algarve in Portugal. The championship will be renamed the ‘Winter Le Mans Series’ as a result.

The change is the latest in a series of alterations to the motorsport calendar which have arisen following the war in the Middle East.

“While moving the Asian Le Mans Series to Europe is not ideal, the situation in the Middle East dictated that we worked to find the best solution,” said series promoter Stephane Ratel. “Between SRO, LMEM and the ACO we have a huge pool of experience to draw on, and the consensus was a Winter Le Mans Series in southern Europe was the most sensible option given the mounting external constraints.”

Formula 1 cancelled its races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia earlier this year. F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali has indicated the series will race in Europe if its final two rounds in the Middle East cannot go ahead.

Sports.title: Daniel Dubois Prepares for New-Look Fabio Wardley
Sports.content:
Dubois (23-3, 22 KOs) posted a photo on Instagram with a group of sparring partners assembled for what may be a tougher fight against former WBO champion Wardley (20-1-1, 19 KOs) than their first meeting on May 9.

The jab wasn’t much of a factor for Wardley in that fight. He loaded up on power shots, swung wildly at times and missed frequently, leaving openings for counters. Wardley still had success with two early knockdowns, but his attacks became easier to read as the rounds progressed.

Wardley is intelligent enough to recognize where he went wrong. Going directly into the second fight gives him a chance to make tactical changes rather than repeat the same approach. He may use his jab more often, shorten his punches and become more selective about when he commits to power shots.

That version of Wardley would give Dubois a different problem to solve. The countering opportunities he found so frequently in May may be harder to find if Wardley fights with greater discipline.

Dubois eventually took control in the second half by landing the cleaner punches and capitalizing on Wardley’s mistakes before stopping him in the 11th round. Starting camp early gives Dubois time to prepare for a more controlled opponent rather than building his strategy around what worked the first time.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson’s Zuffa Debut Could Feature Rayo Valenzuela
Sports.content:
Keith Idec reported Friday in The Ring that Stevenson seems increasingly likely to face Valenzuela next if a fight with WBO welterweight champion Devin Haney remains off the table.

Rayo Valenzuela (16-3, 10 KOs) strengthened his position with a second-round knockout of Edwin De Los Santos in their June 28 rematch in Las Vegas. De Los Santos stopped Valenzuela in three rounds in 2022 before later losing a decision to Stevenson.

De Los Santos had been out of the ring for a lengthy period before the rematch, but Valenzuela still produced the type of finish that makes him an attractive choice. Rayo carries real one-punch power and already competes at 140 pounds.

His loss to WBA champion Gary Antuanne Russell remains the obvious criticism. Russell dominated Valenzuela in March 2025, using constant pressure to prevent him from settling into the fight.

Valenzuela, 27, has since returned with wins over Diego Torres and De Los Santos. Russell also presents a much different style from Shakur, making that defeat an imperfect guide for how Rayo would perform against the WBO titleholder.

Russell would offer Stevenson the chance to add another belt, but Valenzuela gives Zuffa an easier fight to make internally. His one-punch power brings danger while avoiding the difficult negotiations that have stalled Stevenson’s attempt to set up a fight with Haney. It’s a different type of contest for Shakur from the ones he’s been taking lately against Teofimo Lopez, William Zepeda and Josh Padley. Those guys don’t possess the same power as Valenzuela.

The fight would also allow Stevenson to make his Zuffa debut before the end of 2026 instead of remaining inactive while waiting for a bigger fight.

Sports.title: Filip Hrgovic Not Impressed By Moses Itauma Hype
Sports.content:
“I think I’m the best opponent he’s faced. I think he’s never been until now in the ring with someone like me, with that kind of experience and endurance, toughness, power. So let’s see how good he is,” Hrgovic told DAZN Boxing. “Everyone says he’s a future superstar, future Lennox Lewis.”

“You believe it as well, though,” Itauma said.

“Let’s see,” Hrgovic said. “We’ll see. I don’t know. For right now, I’m not impressed. I must see something more than this to believe he’s the real deal. So, let’s see.”

Hrgovic believes he can force Itauma into situations previous opponents have been unable to create. The young heavyweight has spent his rapid climb through the division overwhelming opposition before being pushed into prolonged, difficult fights.

Hrgovic has already experienced those kinds of battles, including his grueling fight with Zhilei Zhang and stoppage loss to Daniel Dubois. His durability gives Itauma something different to solve if the fight extends beyond the early rounds.

Itauma has looked considerably faster than Hrgovic and carries dangerous power, but the Croatian represents a significant jump from the opposition the prospect has faced so far.

The Lennox Lewis comparisons are especially premature. Itauma does not need to resemble a future Hall of Famer on August 29. He does need to show that his talent remains effective against a durable heavyweight capable of absorbing punishment and firing back.

Sports.title: Daniel Dubois-Fabio Wardley Rematch Could Land October 17
Sports.content:
Dubois stopped Wardley in the 11th round of their May 9 fight in Manchester following an exhausting battle in which both heavyweights had difficult moments. Wardley dropped Dubois twice early, putting himself in position to take control before Dubois worked his way back into the fight.

Dubois gradually took over as the rounds passed, landing the cleaner, heavier punches while Wardley absorbed increasing damage. The punishment accumulated before Dubois forced the stoppage in the 11th.

Wardley exercised his contractual right to an immediate rematch rather than taking an interim fight. An October 17 return would leave him with little time to recover physically before beginning another training camp for the same opponent.

That decision recently drew criticism from former two-division champion Paulie Malignaggi, who questioned the wisdom of going directly back into another fight with Dubois. Malignaggi believes Wardley has the punching power to change a fight instantly but sees a considerable skill advantage for Dubois.

The possible October date makes Malignaggi’s concern more relevant. Wardley would have to recover physically, make tactical adjustments and prepare for another demanding heavyweight fight just over five months after the first one.

A quick return also gives Dubois an opportunity to repeat his first result before Wardley has much time to make major changes. Wardley has already shown that he can hurt Dubois. Five months may not be enough to correct the technical weaknesses Dubois exploited as their first fight progressed.

Sports.title: Héctor Camacho Overwhelms Rafael Limón for First World Title
Sports.content:
The belt became available after the WBC stripped Bobby Chacon when a defense against No. 1 contender Camacho failed to materialize. Limón, 29, had recently held the championship before losing a brutal 15-round decision to Chacon in their celebrated fourth fight eight months earlier.

This was Camacho’s first opportunity to win a world title. Limón also represented something new for the young Puerto Rican: an opponent who had previously worn a world championship belt.

The difference in speed became apparent almost immediately. Limón tried to reach Camacho with wide punches, while the younger fighter attacked from different angles, with his straight left finding the target repeatedly. A clean left floored Limón late in the third round. More punishment followed during the fourth as Camacho had him in serious trouble.

Limón’s situation deteriorated further in the fifth. Body shots put him on the canvas in the center of the ring. He regained his feet, but Camacho quickly resumed his assault. A subsequent barrage knocked Limón through the ropes near his corner.

Limón climbed back into position once more. Referee Richard Steele decided he had absorbed enough punishment and stopped the contest at 2:52 of the fifth round. Camacho was the new WBC junior lightweight champion.

All three judges had Camacho comfortably in front through four completed rounds. Dimas Hernandez scored it 40-34, while Moises Sister and Hector Chaumont each had it 40-35.

The celebration afterward illustrated Camacho’s popularity as much as the fight itself. Spectators and members of his entourage poured around the ring as Puerto Rico celebrated its newest world champion.

The performance showed a version of Camacho that later generations of boxing fans rarely saw. Before age and years in the ring changed his style, Camacho possessed extraordinary speed, reflexes and offensive ability. Limón was a hardened former two-time champion who had survived wars with Bobby Chacon, yet the 21-year-old Camacho overwhelmed him with a combination of speed and aggression that Limón simply could not handle.

Camacho made one defense of the title, knocking out Rafael Solis in five rounds, before moving up in weight. Two years after defeating Limón, he captured the WBC lightweight championship. His flamboyant personality, exceptional speed and success across multiple divisions eventually established “Macho” among boxing’s most recognizable stars.

Sports.title: Dwight Braxton Dominates Saad Muhammad In Philadelphia Rematch
Sports.content:
This time, Braxton was even more dominant. Braxton, 29, gave away considerable height and reach to the 28-year-old Saad Muhammad, but the physical disadvantages meant little once the action began. The 5’6″ titleholder worked his way inside behind his jab, forcing the taller challenger onto his back foot.

Saad Muhammad had replaced longtime trainer Sam Solomon with Steve Traitz following the first loss, but the change did little to alter the outcome.

Braxton bloodied Saad Muhammad’s nose in the second round and dropped him in the third. There would be none of the remarkable recoveries that had defined Saad Muhammad’s prime years. Braxton kept attacking with compact hooks, right hands, and heavy body shots.

By the end of five rounds, judges Tony Castellano, Tony Perez, and Dick Young had Braxton comfortably in front by scores of 50-43, 50-42, and 50-41.

The finish came quickly in the sixth. Braxton drove Saad Muhammad toward the ropes with a left-right combination and continued firing as the challenger struggled to defend himself. Referee Carlos Padilla intervened at 1:23, giving Braxton his second consecutive stoppage over his rival.

The performance established Braxton, who would become known as Dwight Muhammad Qawi, as the premier 175-pound fighter alongside Michael Spinks. He later defeated Eddie Davis before losing a light heavyweight unification contest to Spinks in 1983.

The night ended Saad Muhammad’s time at the top of the division. His championship years had featured extraordinary rallies and grueling wars, but those battles took their toll. He continued fighting long after the Braxton losses and was eventually inducted into the International Boxing Hall of Fame.

There was no miraculous Matthew Saad Muhammad comeback this night. Braxton’s inside control, compact punching, and relentless pressure produced an emphatic conclusion to a rivalry he had already taken command of seven months earlier.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Is Running Out Of Fighters To Reject
Sports.content:
The back-and-forth with WBO welterweight champion Devin Haney illustrates the problem. Shakur wants a 144-pound catchweight, a condition Bill Haney rejected by insisting Devin should not drop below the 147-pound welterweight limit.

Shakur can take the fight at 147, pursue a mandatory position or move on to another opponent. Instead, another potentially lucrative fight has stalled because he wants terms the champion has little reason to accept.

That is almost the opposite of the old-school mentality. Fighters who scored career-defining wins often returned to work quickly, signing another fight and capitalizing on their success while the public was still talking about them.

Seven months is enough time to negotiate a deal, complete a training camp and fight again. Shakur has instead acted like an employee who had the best day of his career at the office and responded by taking an extended vacation.

Shakur spent years trying to reach this position. The question now is how many months of his prime he’s willing to sacrifice by ruling out opponents and demanding terms that keep fights from getting made.

Sports.title: Murat Gassiev Vs Jarrell Miller Talks Underway For WBA Belt
Sports.content:
“There’s a little bit of confusion with the WBA. I mean, Gassiev’s the champion. He’s got to fight Jarrell Miller, our guy, which we’re negotiating at the moment,” Hearn told iFL TV.

The fight offers Miller a shot at a heavyweight belt late in his career. A scheduled 2019 title bout against Anthony Joshua was canceled after Miller failed multiple drug tests before the event.

Miller rebuilt his career and remains a difficult opponent due to his size, constant pressure, and high work rate. A fight against Gassiev puts him near the top of the division without requiring a long series of elimination bouts.

Gassiev’s heavyweight run has moved slowly since leaving the cruiserweight division. The former unified cruiserweight champion possesses considerable punching power, though health issues and long layoffs have prevented him from establishing the same position at heavyweight that he held at 200 pounds.

Hearn is already considering potential opponents if Miller wins.

“Hopefully Jarrell Miller can beat Gassiev. We can do Miller against Kabayel. There’s loads of fights to be made,” Hearn said.

Miller first needs the Gassiev fight finalized. At 38, an opportunity to challenge a WBA champion gives the recently signed Matchroom heavyweight another chance to capture a world title.

Ghana News.title: Is the “Democracy Under Attack” narrative real, or is it a convenient escape from accountability?
Ghana News.content:
The opposition has marched in red and black, chanting that democracy is under attack. The slogans are loud, the placards are colourful, and the cameras are rolling. But beneath the spectacle lies a simple question: What exactly is under attack?

Is democracy under attack because former public officials are being investigated over decisions they took while exercising public power? If accountability has suddenly become oppression, then every anti-corruption institution should probably close shop.

Is democracy under attack because people who allegedly spread falsehoods or make threatening statements are invited to answer before the law? Freedom of expression has never included a licence to publish anything without consequence. Rights exist alongside responsibilities.

Or is democracy under attack because political actors who once wielded the full machinery of the state now find themselves on the receiving end of the same legal processes they once defended?

There is a certain irony in watching those who once insisted that "the law must take its course" suddenly discover the vocabulary of victimhood when the law knocks on their own doors.

This is not to suggest that any government is above criticism. Every administration must be scrutinised, and every abuse of power must be resisted. Democracy thrives on dissent. But democracy also thrives on consistency. If accountability was patriotic yesterday, it cannot become persecution simply because the names on the docket have changed.

The greatest weakness of the "Democracy Under Attack" narrative is that it asks Ghanaians to suffer from selective amnesia. Citizens remember the years when journalists complained of intimidation, when critics accused the state of heavy-handedness, and when public confidence in governance steadily declined. Those memories cannot simply be erased with matching T-shirts and dramatic slogans.

Even more striking is the leadership presenting itself as the guardian of democratic values. A party once admired for discipline, intellectual depth, and organisational strength increasingly appears trapped between defending its past and explaining its present. Rather than offering a compelling alternative vision, it seems preoccupied with portraying accountability as oppression.

Of course, every political party has the constitutional right to demonstrate. Peaceful protest is itself an expression of democratic freedom. Ironically, the very ability to organise nationwide demonstrations, criticise the government publicly, and march through the streets under police protection is evidence that democratic space continues to exist.

Perhaps the demonstration was less about saving democracy and more about energising a discouraged political base. There is nothing inherently wrong with mobilising supporters. Political parties do it everywhere. But dressing ordinary political mobilisation in the robes of a constitutional emergency risks diminishing genuine threats to democracy when they actually arise.

Democracy is not endangered because former officeholders are called upon to account for their stewardship. We need a vigilant and constructive opposition not those full of hypocrisy. We deserve robust criticism of government and principled defenders of constitutionalism in honesty.

If every investigation becomes "persecution," every prosecution becomes "dictatorship," and every legal process becomes "an attack on democracy," then the phrase itself loses all meaning.

Sometimes the loudest cries of "Save Democracy" are really pleas to save politicians from accountability.

Ghana News.title: Car dealer shot dead, wife critically injured in attack at Tuba Beach Drive Estate
Ghana News.content:
A 50-year-old car dealer has been shot dead, while his wife is in critical condition after unidentified gunmen attacked the couple outside their home at Beach Drive Estate near Tuba in the Ga South Municipality of the Greater Accra Region.

The deceased, Kwesi Rahman, was reportedly returning home with his wife from an evening walk when the incident occurred at about 9:30 p.m. on Thursday, August 6.

According to eyewitnesses, the couple had just arrived at the entrance to their residence when an unidentified assailant emerged and opened fire on them.

Mr. Rahman sustained multiple gunshot wounds and died instantly at the scene, while his wife was also shot several times.

Residents who heard the gunfire rushed to the scene and assisted in transporting the injured woman to a nearby hospital, where she is receiving treatment. For security and medical reasons, the facility where she is being treated has not been disclosed.

Speaking to Adom News, an eyewitness, Faustina Antwi, said the body of the deceased had been conveyed to the police morgue for preservation and autopsy.

A resident who witnessed the aftermath of the attack said the sound of gunfire sent residents rushing from their homes.

“I was outside around 9:50 when I heard what sounded like a gunshot. So I quickly went inside and told my mum that I had heard gunshots. When we came out, we saw people coming from down there. When I got there, I saw him lying in front of his gate. I didn’t see anybody and I didn’t hear any noise. It was just the gunshot I heard,” the resident recounted.

The incident has left residents of Beach Drive Estate shaken, with many expressing concern over security in the community.

Some residents have called on the Ghana Police Service to intensify security patrols within the estate to protect lives and property and restore confidence among residents.

A relative of the deceased also appealed to the police to conduct a thorough investigation to identify those responsible and bring them to justice.

Police have since launched investigations into the shooting and are working to identify and arrest the gunman behind the attack.

Mr. Rahman, who celebrated his 50th birthday in July this year, was well known in the community as a car dealer. Authorities are yet to establish the motive behind the attack.

Ghana News.title: US appeals court halts Trump ballroom project paving way for Supreme Court showdown
Ghana News.content:
The Trump administration has been ordered to stop construction on President Donald Trump's $400m (£297m) ballroom at the White House.

A federal appeals court dealt the latest setback to the controversial project on Friday, testing Trump's presidential authority and paving the way for a Supreme Court showdown on appeal.

"Whether or not a ⁠massive ballroom should be constructed is for Congress to decide and is not a matter for Executive self-help," the panel's ​majority said.

The order upholds a preliminary ​injunction won by the National Trust for Historic Preservation, which sued after the administration tore down the ​East Wing last year to begin the project without congressional approval.

"Congress has not ceded unfettered authority to the Executive Branch to dramatically redesign, reshape, and reconstruct the White House — the People's ​House — to fit a particular President's desires," the panel said.

The three-judge panel, in a 2-1 decision, said: "Each President is a temporary tenant, not the owner, of the White House and its Executive Residence."

"The President has no — and claims no — constitutionally assigned authority over that property, which is designed and maintained for the use of all Presidents, current and future, and for the American people," the opinion said.

The administration appealed to the court after a federal judge twice blocked above-ground construction on the ballroom, while still allowing underground work to proceed.

The ruling on Friday upholds that order blocking above-ground construction without congressional approval. The appeals court delayed implementation of its ruling for 14 days to allow the Trump administration to appeal to the Supreme Court.

The BBC has contacted the White House and Department of Justice for comment.

Construction at the site where the East Wing previously stood was previously ordered to stop, but a court delayed the ruling allowing construction to continue while the appeals court considered briefs and heard arguments last month, according to the BBC's US media partner CBS.

President Trump has asserted that the new ballroom is needed to "accommodate people for grand parties, State Visits", and has also said that it is "vital for National Security".

He doubled down on the need for the space after an assassination attempt at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner in April.

The three-judge panel on Friday said that its ruling "has nothing at all to do with whether the proposed ballroom is desirable", nor does it weigh in on whether the administration may ultimately construct the ballroom.

"What it does mean is that the Defendants may not do so during the district court's expeditious litigation without securing Congress's authorization, as the Constitution and laws require," the order said.

The National Trust for Historic Preservation celebrated the latest ruling, noting that no above-ground construction can take place "unless and until" Congress takes action.

"The White House, a global landmark that symbolizes American identity and the ideals of democracy, belongs to the American people," said Brent Leggs, President and CEO of the National Trust.

"The National Trust for Historic Preservation and its partners are proud to defend this irreplaceable monument on behalf of all Americans."

Ghana News.title: Crickets in the theatre and leaking wards: How Lawra Hospital is battling century-old decay to save lives
Ghana News.content:
The Lawra Municipal Hospital, a 98-year-old facility in the Upper West Region, is battling severe infrastructural decay, with medical staff recently forced to conduct emergency surgeries amid invading insects and deliver babies in wards with leaking roofs.

Established in 1928, the historic hospital has undergone no major renovations since its inception. A financial crisis, driven by low Out-Patient Department (OPD) attendance and mounting legacy debts, has left the facility struggling to procure basic medical consumables. However, targeted interventions by the Member of Parliament for the Lawra Constituency, Bede Anwataazumo Ziedeng, are offering a glimmer of hope to the overstretched medical staff.

Before the MP's recent intervention to refurbish the hospital's operating theatre, the surgical team faced a terrifying reality.

Mohammed Muslim, a nurse and deputy in charge of the theatre, disclosed that the facility previously relied on wooden doors and louvre windows, which failed to keep the theatre airtight.

"Sometimes, especially during the night, when you are on duty, you could see insects, even crickets, enter the main theatre," Muslim recalled.

He noted the serious risk this posed to patients, warning that if an insect found its way into a patient's open abdomen during surgery, it could cause life-threatening infections.

Following a passionate appeal by the hospital management, the MP replaced the wooden doors and louvre windows with airtight doors and windows and has yet to install new air conditioners.

"Once all those things are changed, we don't experience those things again," Muslim added with relief.

While the theatre has seen significant improvements, the maternity and gynaecology wards remain in a deplorable state, turning the rainy season into a nightmare for expectant mothers.

Aysha Goodman, Deputy Chief Midwifery Officer for Public Health, revealed that the roof of the gynaecology ward leaks heavily, allowing rainwater to pour directly onto patients' beds.

"Anytime it's raining, the clients cannot lie on their bed; they have to shift and pair with other clients," Madam Goodman lamented.

She said the poor conditions are forcing some pregnant women who require admission to seek care elsewhere.

The infrastructural challenges in the maternity ward are compounded by a shortage of essential logistics, including bedsheets, mattresses and an ultrasound machine. In emergencies, nurses are often forced to wheel pregnant women to another part of the hospital, or even outside the facility, to undergo ultrasound scans before they can be taken into theatre.

"And then some of the... like scan machines for our clients. At times, when a pregnant woman comes here, we need to do scan before going to theatre. We have to push the person to the other side, or outside the hospital for scan. So that one too is our challenge in this hospital."

Before the MP's recent donation of GH¢100,000 worth of non-drug consumables, including gloves and syringes, staff were also compelled to ask emergency patients to purchase their own surgical supplies from pharmacies in town before treatment could begin.

Despite these difficult conditions, the dedicated midwives at the Lawra Municipal Hospital have achieved a remarkable feat by recording zero maternal deaths for four consecutive years.

However, the Medical Superintendent, Dr Ziblila Musah, said the persistent infrastructural and logistical challenges continue to affect staff morale.

While acknowledging the MP's continuous support, Dr Musah appealed to the government, the District Assembly and philanthropists to urgently renovate the ageing facility and provide the equipment needed to improve healthcare delivery.

"Providing these logistics and making the working environment conducive is a motivation to staff," Dr Musah stressed. "And when we get all that, we are going to put in our best."

Ghana News.title: NALAG President throws down the challenge: Deliver development or lose public trust
Ghana News.content:
President of the National Association of Local Authorities of Ghana (NALAG), Alfred Asiedu Adjei, has issued a stern warning to Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies (MMDAs), saying local government officials risk losing public confidence if they fail to deliver visible development and accountable leadership.



Addressing the Ashanti Regional Conference of Presiding Members in Kumasi, Mr Adjei said citizens are no longer willing to judge local authorities by promises and political rhetoric but by tangible improvements in their communities.



"Local governance is changing across the world. Citizens are no longer satisfied with promises alone. They want results. They want leaders who listen. They want transparency in the use of public resources. They want Assemblies that are responsive to their needs," he said.



Speaking on the theme, "Leading Change at the Grassroots: The Role of Presiding Members," the NALAG President challenged Presiding Members to redefine leadership by ensuring Assembly decisions translate into improved roads, better sanitation, quality healthcare, education, employment opportunities and effective flood control.



He said the credibility of local government institutions now depends on their ability to solve everyday problems confronting citizens.



"Communities do not remember leaders for the offices they occupied. They remember them for the problems they solved," Mr Adjei stated.



He urged Presiding Members to move beyond presiding over Assembly meetings and instead provide leadership that promotes consensus, accountability and development.



According to him, every Assembly committee must function efficiently, every decision must reflect fairness and the public interest, and every resolution must produce measurable benefits for local communities.



Hon. Adjei also called for greater transparency in the management of public resources, stressing that restoring public trust requires Assemblies to deepen citizen participation, strengthen financial accountability and openly account for public funds.



Looking to the future of decentralisation, he advocated the adoption of digital technology, data-driven planning and improved mobilisation of internally generated revenue to enhance service delivery.



He further called on Assemblies to mainstream environmental sustainability, disaster preparedness and inclusive governance by ensuring women, youth and persons with disabilities are fully represented in local decision-making.



The NALAG President reaffirmed the Association's commitment to improving the welfare of Assembly Members and Presiding Members through advocacy for timely payment of allowances, enhanced logistics, capacity building and better working conditions.



He said strengthening the capacity and welfare of local government officials was essential to building institutions capable of delivering effective governance.



Mr. Adjei reminded participants that Ghana's national development would ultimately be determined by the performance of its local governments.



"When our Assemblies succeed, our districts succeed. When our districts succeed, our regions succeed. And when our regions succeed, Ghana succeeds," he said.

Ghana News.title: Let’s focus on the job – Vice President dismisses 2028 NDC flagbearer speculation
Ghana News.content:
Vice President Prof. Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang has dismissed early discussions about the National Democratic Congress' (NDC) 2028 presidential candidate, urging party members to concentrate on delivering on the government's mandate.

Speaking on The KSM Show on Friday, August 7, the Vice President said it was too early to engage in succession debates, stressing that the party was elected to solve the country's challenges rather than campaign for the next election.

Responding to questions about whether she intends to contest the NDC's flagbearer position, Prof. Opoku-Agyemang said the party's future electoral prospects depend on the performance of the current administration and the support given to President John Dramani Mahama.

"Whether we are going or coming depends on the work we are doing. It depends on the support we are giving our president who's leading the charge," she said.

She cautioned that premature discussions about the party's next flagbearer could distract the government from its responsibilities.

"If we are already going left or right, and centre and back, and it's not even time, I think it's a betrayal of the cause of the people, and I don't think it is right," she said. "Please help us to fulfil the dreams of this beautiful country. Let's focus on getting the job done."

The Vice President also noted that the NDC's victory in the 2024 general election was the result of years of hard work and should not be overshadowed by early political maneuvering.

Ghana News.title: Former TOR MD and Goldman Sachs investment banker convicted of foreign bribery, money laundering
Ghana News.content:
Asante Kwaku Berko, a dual citizen of the United States and Ghana, was convicted today by a federal jury in Brooklyn on all counts of an indictment charging conspiracy to violate the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA), violating the FCPA, and money laundering conspiracy for paying bribes to Ghanaian government officials in connection with the development of a power plant in Ghana.

The verdict followed a nine-day trial before United States District Judge Diane Gujarati. When sentenced, Berko faces up to 30 years in prison. Berko was ordered remanded pending sentencing.

Joseph Nocella, Jr., United States Attorney for the Eastern District of New York, A. Tysen Duva, Assistant Attorney General of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division, and James C. Barnacle, Jr., Assistant Director in Charge, Federal Bureau of Investigation, New York Field Office, announced the verdict.

“Today’s verdict marks another significant victory in this Office’s longstanding commitment to rooting out corruption,” stated United States Attorney Nocella. “The defendant abused his access to high-level foreign government officials and his platform as an investment banker at a prestigious American firm to line his own pockets with millions of dollars.”

“We live in a global economy that American companies must be able to compete in fairly,” said Assistant Attorney General Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “This defendant corrupted that fair competition. He abused his position at a world-renowned American investment bank by helping bribe Ghanaian officials, so he and his co-conspirators, including senior executives at a Turkish company, could make money. Today’s conviction makes clear that criminals who undermine our country’s interests by corrupting foreign governments and cutting off fair competition will face the full force of the Department of Justice.”

“Today’s verdict highlights the importance of domestic and international partnerships, and the magnitude of success that working together creates. The FBI is thankful for the assistance from the Department of Justice and the United Kingdom – specifically to the Office of International Affairs, U.S. Marshals Service, and INTERPOL – in pursuing justice to protect our country’s financial integrity,” stated FBI Assistant Director in Charge Barnacle.

U.S. Attorney Nocella also expressed his appreciation to the Government of the United Kingdom, the U.K. National Centre Bureau for INTERPOL, the Embassy of the United States in London, the Department’s Office of International Affairs and the U.S. Marshals Service for providing substantial assistance in securing the arrest and extradition of the defendant.

As proved at trial, Berko conspired to pay more than $1 million in bribes to multiple Ghanian government officials in connection with the development and financing of a power plant estimated to generate hundreds of millions of dollars in profits.

Beginning in December 2014, Berko, a former Executive Director in the Investment Banking Division at Goldman Sachs group, was responsible for securing and managing a deal between the Republic of Ghana and Aksa Enerji Uretim A.S. (Aksa), a Turkish energy company and Goldman client, for the construction and financing of a power plant in Ghana amidst a national energy crisis in the country.

During the scheme, Berko and his co-conspirators paid and conspired to pay bribes to individuals at numerous levels of the Ghanaian government to ensure that Aksa won its bid to build and operate the power plant. For example, in April 2015, Berko and the conspirators discussed paying $1 million to the Ghanaian Minister of Power who was responsible for securing key approvals enabling the project to progress and $250,000 to his senior adviser. Bribes were also paid to five Ghanaian officials during an all-expenses-paid trip to Turkey to view equipment for the power plant. After the power plant deal was ratified by the Ghanaian parliament in July 2015, Berko and his co-conspirators exchanged detailed emails regarding bribe payments. For example, in August 2015, they discussed $250,000 in bribe payments paid to various individuals, including $46,000 to members of the Ghanaian Parliament, which ratified the agreement between Aksa and the government of Ghana, paid by Berko himself. Also in August 2015, the co-conspirators discussed how a bribe recipient was waiting for the “holy rain” (i.e., the bribe payment) and “would appreciate it sooner rather than later.”

To conceal the scheme from Goldman and others, Berko lied to the compliance team at Goldman that was responsible for vetting the deal. Berko also used his personal email account, instead of his Goldman business email account, to discuss the deal and the bribe payments and directed his co-conspirators to do the same. In addition, Berko and his co-conspirators concealed and laundered the bribe payments using shell companies, sham invoices, nominee account holders and cash withdrawals. Payments in furtherance of the bribery scheme were laundered through U.S. and foreign bank accounts. Goldman ultimately withdrew from the deal due to corruption concerns.

The government’s case is being handled by the Business and Securities Fraud Section of the United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of New York and the Criminal Division’s Fraud Section. Assistant United States Attorneys Jessica Weigel, Nick M. Axelrod and Tara McGrath are prosecuting the case with Assistant Chief Katherine Raut and Senior Trial Attorney Katherine Nielsen, and with assistance from Paralegal Specialists Melina Piatti-Chayan, Isha Jayadev and Teresa Dolan.

Ghana News.title: Into The Unknown Tours embarks on 10-day Journey to the North
Ghana News.content:
Into The Unknown Tours will embark on a 10-day road expedition from Accra to Tamale to spotlight lesser-known destinations and promote domestic tourism.

Dubbed Journey to the North, the expedition begins on Friday, 14 August 2026, and runs until Sunday, 23 August, taking the team from Accra through the Volta Region before continuing into Northern Ghana.

The content-driven adventure will document breathtaking landscapes, historic landmarks, local culture, cuisine and the people who make each destination unique, with daily content shared across social media.

The expedition is in partnership with CFAO Mobility Ghana and Malta Guinness, with the two brands supporting the journey as the official mobility and beverage partners respectively.

CFAO Mobility Ghana is providing a fleet of vehicles that will power the entire journey. The convoy will include the adventurous Suzuki Jimny, the rugged Mitsubishi L200 pickup and the versatile Mitsubishi Pajero Sport, each selected to confidently navigate the varied roads and terrain the team will encounter over the 10-day expedition.

Joining the journey as the official beverage partner, Malta Guinness will support the crew throughout the expedition, reinforcing its long-standing association with resilience, energy and the spirit of achievement.

The expedition aims to shift the narrative around domestic tourism by showing that some of Ghana’s most remarkable experiences exist far beyond the country’s most familiar tourist attractions.

Leading the expedition is Derrick Boateng, CEO of Into The Unknown Tours, whose passion for discovering untold stories has helped build a growing community of adventure lovers across Ghana.

“There are incredible places in Ghana that many of us have never seen. Our goal is to tell those stories, inspire travel, and remind Ghanaians that adventure doesn’t always require a passport,” Derrick said.

The 10-day expedition follows the success of the brand’s previous content journey to Nzulezu, which generated millions of online impressions and sparked renewed interest in domestic tourism.

This year’s expedition will take audiences through towns including Ho, Hohoe, Jasikan, Kadjebi, Yendi, Savelugu and Tamale, with daily content showcasing the country’s diverse landscapes and cultures.

Beyond inspiring travel, the initiative also seeks to shine a spotlight on local businesses, hotels, restaurants, tourist attractions and communities along the route, creating visibility and economic opportunities through digital storytelling.

Speaking about the partnerships, Derrick Boateng, CEO of Into The Unknown Tours, described them as a defining moment for the organisation.

“Having the support of CFAO Mobility Ghana and Malta Guinness is an incredible vote of confidence in our vision. Together, we’re proving that Ghana has countless stories waiting to be discovered, and we’re excited to share them with the country and the world.”

With domestic tourism becoming an increasingly important contributor to Ghana’s economy, initiatives like Journey to the North demonstrate how content creators can play a significant role in promoting national heritage while encouraging citizens to explore more of their country.

Followers will be able to experience the journey in real time across Into The Unknown Tours’ social media platforms.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Mediterranean smuggling network ‘dismantled’ in Spain-led raid, 78 arrested
World.content:
Authorities say they broke up one of the largest criminal networks running migrant smuggling in the Western Mediterranean.

Spanish authorities, working with Europol and police in France, Portugal and Poland, have dismantled what they say is one of the largest criminal networks for migrant smuggling, illegal drugs and weapons trafficking across the Western Mediterranean.

Launched by Spain’s Civil Guard and National Police in 2023, the operation culminated in an “action day” on June 16, Europol said on Friday, leading to 78 arrests and the seizure of assets, including 18 high-speed boats.

Officials described the crossings as extremely dangerous, with migrants crammed into overcrowded boats travelling at high speed through rough seas, often without lighting or life jackets.

Authorities said passengers were sometimes tied down to keep them from falling overboard, and that the organisation used extraordinary violence against migrants, its own members and police.

The operation “successfully dismantled one of the ⁠most complex, active and dangerous transnational criminal networks detected to date in the Mediterranean,” Spain’s Civil Guard said in a statement.

Of those detained, 77 were arrested in Spain and one in Algeria, including three high-value targets. Most were Algerian nationals with ties to criminal groups in France, Belgium, Portugal, Italy and Poland.

As part of the operation, 17 locations were searched in Spain, including in Alicante, Almeria, Cartagena and Murcia.

The announcement on Friday comes a week after a mass migrant surge into Spain’s North African enclave of Ceuta drew international attention to migration pressures in the region.



The criminal network, described as operating like a logistics company for organised crime groups, managed two-way maritime smuggling routes between Europe and Algeria, according to Europol.

The network allegedly moved synthetic drugs southward and migrants northward to Spain’s southeastern coast and the island of Ibiza.

Investigators say the network carried out at least 64 migrant-smuggling operations, bringing more than 2,000 people into Spain and generating over €24 million ($27m) in profits, charging as much as €12,000 ($13,800) per migrant and packing up to 50 people onto a single boat.

Authorities also found that the network provided a wide range of services to other criminal organisations, including vessel storage, transportation, refuelling, maritime transfers, boat maintenance and counter-surveillance.

The network reportedly moved money through informal hawala networks, making it difficult for investigators to trace illicit funds.

World.title: Hun Manet is refining Cambodia’s authoritarian model
World.content:
When Hun Sen handed Cambodia’s premiership to his eldest son, Hun Manet, in August 2023, many diplomats and regional observers saw the succession as an opportunity for change. The carefully stage-managed handover fuelled hopes that a new generation of leaders, headed by a prime minister educated at West Point, New York University and the University of Bristol, might reopen Cambodia’s political space after decades of authoritarian rule.

Writing at the time, I argued that this optimism was misplaced, not because the leadership was changing, but because the political system was not. Western policymakers were eager to believe that a dynastic transfer might create room to recalibrate relations with Phnom Penh. But they failed to recognise how deeply the Cambodian People’s Party’s survival depended on preserving the very institutions that had forced opposition figures such as me into exile. Hun Sen’s sweeping crackdowns on the opposition, independent media and civil society were not aberrations, but expressions of a governing model he had built and the ruling elite continued to sustain: one based on patronage, coercion and the elimination of political competition. As long as that model remained intact, there was little reason to expect a new leader to rule any differently.

Three years on, this assessment has been borne out. Hun Manet has not governed as the liberal reformer many hoped he would. Instead, he has preserved the foundations of his father’s rule while making its repressive machinery less visible and more institutionally sophisticated. Although violence has become less conspicuous, the regime increasingly relies on elite patronage, legal repression, digital surveillance and tighter control over communications. The result is a quieter but arguably more resilient authoritarian state.



This technocratic upgrade is perhaps most visible in the regime’s treatment of civil society. In July 2024, five of Mother Nature’s young leaders – Ly Chandaravuth, Long Kunthea, Phuon Keoraksmey, Thun Ratha and Yim Leanghy – were sentenced to between six and eight years in prison on trumped-up charges including “conspiring against the state” and “insulting the king”. Their real offence was exposing environmental destruction and corruption, including illegal logging and sand-mining operations that directly enrich the ruling elite. Today, they remain in overcrowded provincial prisons across the country, effectively isolated from their families and legal counsel, with their appeals delayed indefinitely.

What remains of Cambodia’s political opposition has faced similar persecution. The Candlelight Party and the Nation Power Party have faced routine legal harassment and administrative obstruction, while their leaders and supporters have been subjected to arbitrary arrests and politically motivated prosecutions, making meaningful electoral competition impossible. Rong Chhun, a veteran labour leader and senior Nation Power Party adviser, was sentenced to four years in prison in 2025. Although the Supreme Court later suspended the remainder of his sentence, it upheld his conviction and barred him from voting or participating in politics for five years.

Independent journalism has fared no better. Reporters investigating corruption, land seizures, illegal logging and the cyber-scam operations that have proliferated across Cambodia operate under constant pressure. In late 2024, environmental journalist Chhoeung Chheng was fatally shot while investigating illegal logging inside a protected wildlife sanctuary. That same year, Mech Dara, who helped expose the country’s role as a global hub for online fraud and human trafficking, was arrested on incitement charges widely viewed as politically motivated. Although Dara was later released on bail, his detention sent a clear warning to journalists investigating the regime’s alleged links to an industry that now generates billions of dollars annually by defrauding victims across Asia, Europe and North America.

Taken together, these developments show that the consolidation of Hun Manet’s rule has brought not a political opening, but just a minor refinement of Cambodia’s authoritarian model. Yet many Western governments continue to pursue diplomatic engagement and offer economic incentives in the hope that sustained dialogue will persuade Cambodia to rebalance its foreign policy and gradually reopen political space. This expectation rests on a fundamental misunderstanding. It treats Cambodia’s growing alignment with China as a foreign-policy preference that can be moderated through engagement, when it has in fact become central to the ruling party’s strategy for preserving power and shielding itself from Western pressure over democracy and human rights. Unlike Western partners, Beijing provides investment, diplomatic backing and security cooperation without demanding democratic reform, giving the ruling party greater room to withstand external pressure.



The depth of this alignment is visible in both Cambodia’s economic and security partnerships with Beijing. The Funan Techo Canal, backed by a $1.2bn financing agreement with Chinese partners, has become emblematic of China’s economic footprint in Cambodia. Chinese investors accounted for 54 percent of the country’s approved investment capital in 2025. The Chinese-funded expansion and reopening of Ream Naval Base point to the same trend. Although Phnom Penh insists the facility remains under Cambodian sovereignty, Chinese financing and construction have fuelled persistent concerns that Beijing is securing a long-term strategic foothold on the Gulf of Thailand. Whatever the base’s eventual military significance, it underscores how deeply China is now embedded in Cambodia’s security architecture.

This reality should prompt a change in Western policy. For too long, Western governments have prioritised diplomatic access over leverage, assuming that technical cooperation and sustained dialogue would gradually encourage political reform and imposing few consequences when that assumption proved false. Future cooperation should instead be explicitly tied to measurable democratic progress. Judicial capacity-building programmes that lend legitimacy to compromised courts should be suspended. Targeted sanctions should be expanded to include officials, military commanders and business elites implicated in serious human rights abuses and Cambodia’s cybercrime economy. Western participation in high-level forums hosted by Cambodia, including the Francophonie Summit in November, should be made contingent on the release of political prisoners, credible action to dismantle scam compounds, an end to politically motivated prosecutions and stronger protections for independent media.

For years, the international community has mistaken generational succession for political reform. Hun Manet’s Cambodia demonstrates that authoritarian systems can modernise without liberalising. Only by recognising that reality can Western governments stop reinforcing the institutions that have closed off democratic competition and begin helping to create the conditions for Cambodia’s democratic renewal.

The views expressed in this article are the author’s own and do not necessarily reflect Al Jazeera’s editorial stance.

World.title: US labour market sheds jobs in July as labour force participation slumps
World.content:
US labour market loses 23,000 jobs in July as education, government and retail sectors record significant declines

The United States labour market lost 23,000 jobs in July, with major declines across several sectors, including education, government and retail trade.

On Friday, the Bureau of Labor Statistics released its latest jobs report, which showed that the unemployment rate fell to 4.1 percent from 4.2 percent.

Part of that dip, however, was driven by a decline in labour force participation, the percentage of people working or actively looking for work.

Labour force participation fell to 61.4 percent, its lowest level in five years. Excluding the economic impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic, the labour force participation rate is at its lowest level in five decades.

Some 264,000 people left the labour force, meaning they are no longer working or looking for work.

The retail trade sector lost 19,000 jobs overall. Warehouse clubs and big-box retailers were hit the hardest, shedding 21,000 jobs, while petrol stations cut another 5,000. Those losses were partly offset by gains at stores selling more specialised goods, such as music and sporting goods stores, which added 10,000 jobs.

During the height of the normally busy summer travel season, the US economy also lost jobs in leisure and hospitality. The sector shed 40,000 jobs, with food services accounting for 26,000 of those losses.

The biggest losses came in government, which shed 53,000 jobs overall. Most of those cuts were in local education, which lost 49,000 jobs.

There were gains in healthcare, with the sector adding 22,000 jobs. Most of those gains were concentrated in ambulatory healthcare services, which added 18,000 jobs.



June’s jobs numbers were also revised in the latest report, with the month now showing a downwardly revised gain of 20,000 jobs.

The latest jobs report comes amid a so-called “low-hire, low-fire” environment, which essentially means that people who have jobs are not leaving them in large numbers to take new positions.

The number of job openings dropped slightly from 7.5 million to 7.4 million in May, while hiring remained unchanged at 5.3 million, according to the Job Openings and Labor Turnover Summary report from the Bureau of Labor Statistics published on Tuesday.

Experts say the recent reports suggest an economic slump, contributing to low confidence among American consumers.

“There’s no sugar coating the overarching message in the July jobs report – the economy is struggling,” Mark Zandi, the chief economist at Moody’s Analytics, a financial services firm, wrote on social media.

Zandi pointed to the slumping labour force participation rate as a “clear tell” of an ailing job market.

“While unemployment is low, that’s only because those losing their jobs are leaving the workforce, too discouraged to look for a job, as few businesses are hiring,” he explained.

With wage growth being outpaced by the pace of inflation, Zandi added, “no wonder most Americans say they are upset about their finances and the economy’s performance”.

Friday’s jobs report is also affecting expectations for the interest rates set by the Federal Reserve. Increasingly, experts expect the US central bank to hold interest rates steady at its next policy meeting in September.

CME’s FedWatch tool, which tracks the likelihood of monetary policy decisions, now forecasts a 56 percent chance that rates will remain unchanged, up from 45 percent on Thursday.

Last month, the Federal Reserve maintained its benchmark interest rate at 3.50 to 3.75 percent.

Despite the jobs data, US markets are on the upswing. The Nasdaq is up 0.9 percent, while the S&P 500 is 0.5 percent higher than at the market open. The Dow Jones Industrial Average is up 0.3 percent in midday trading.

The price of gold, which is typically considered a safe-haven investment during times of economic uncertainty, is up 2.2 percent at $4,336.09 an ounce.
