World.title: Italy vows to maintain border checks despite Spain’s countermeasures threat
World.content:
Madrid warns of ‘proportional measures’ if Rome does not put an end to checks amid fallout from Ceuta migrant crisis.

How the far right weaponised the Ceuta crisis

Italy has doubled down on its temporary reinstatement of border controls following the deadly rush of thousands of migrants into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, even after Madrid threatened retaliation.

In a statement on Friday, the Italian government said it would not bow to “ultimatums or impositions” from ⁠Spain and would maintain border controls until at least August 15.

The refusal came hours after the Spanish government declared a two-day deadline for Italy “to rectify, put an end to the checks and treat Spaniards like other European citizens”.

“If it does not do so before the end of Sunday, August 9, Spain will be obliged to adopt proportional measures to protect the interests and dignity of its citizens,” Spain’s statement said.

The diplomatic tit-for-tat unfolds as Spain continues to reel from the influx of some 72,000 people who crossed into Ceuta from Morocco last week, on foot and by sea.

Mass arrivals in the North African Spanish enclave angered other European Union leaders who have taken a hard anti-migration stance, including far-right Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni.

Italy earlier said it would temporarily reintroduce border checks with Spain starting on August 1 in what Meloni called an “extraordinary measure” seeking to “safeguard national security and prevent possible repercussions for our nation”.

Yet experts said there was little prospect of migrants travelling from Ceuta to Italy, particularly as Italy and Spain do not share a land border. Rights groups instead pegged Meloni’s move as “political theatre”.



Still, 22 EU member states signed a joint letter accusing Spain of “pull factors” that destabilise the bloc’s borders.

The vast majority of the Ceuta migrants have since returned to Morocco as authorities tallied at least 100 deaths.

Also on Friday, Spain said its police successfully dismantled a people-smuggling operation believed to have brought 2,000 migrants into the country via Spain’s southeastern coast and the island of Ibiza.

Unaccompanied minors

Amid the political fallout, Spanish leaders are grappling with a humanitarian crisis still ongoing in Ceuta.

Of the few thousand undocumented migrants who remain in the enclave, at least 1,342 are children, Youth Minister Sira Rego said on Friday – hundreds of whom are unaccompanied.

Rego acknowledged “painful images” of children sleeping on Ceuta’s streets, noting that two schools had been opened as authorities evaluated more locations as possible reception centres.

Still, Ceuta authorities said at least 1,100 children needed assistance, with Ceuta’s theoretical capacity only totalling 90 places where people could be housed.

“It might only be a matter of a few weeks before we start seeing [children] transferred to and welcomed on the mainland,” Rego told reporters.

Local and international charities have cautioned that the children face abuse and exploitation.

Jose Miguel Morales, head of Federacion Sur Acoge, a migrant rights and assistance group in southern Spain, said some of the children were under 14 years old and had already been beaten and assaulted.

But the transfer of children to the mainland has become a domestic flashpoint in Madrid, where Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez’s government approved 25 million euros ($29m) to help support unaccompanied minors in the territory.

Leaders from the far-right, anti-immigration Vox party were quick to say they opposed any aid for migrant children.

Vox leader Santiago Abascal wrote on X that “not one euro from Spaniards” should go “for illegals, for invaders”.

World.title: Sri Lanka prisoners riot leaving 3 dead, 23 injured in chaos
World.content:
Authorities suspect narcotics dealers and gang rivalries are behind prison violence at several facilities in Sri Lanka.

Police and riot squads have been deployed after three inmates were killed and nearly two dozen others were injured in separate prison riots across Sri Lanka.

Public Security Minister Ananda Wijepala told parliament on Friday that one prisoner was killed when 40 inmates broke out of their cells at the New Magazine Prison in the capital, Colombo, late on Thursday.

Two more prisoners were killed on Friday morning during a second riot at Kuruwita prison, about 80km (50 miles) from the capital, he said.

Between the two incidents, 23 inmates were injured and admitted to hospitals, Wijepala said, adding that police and special forces ‌brought both riots under control.

Additionally, police told the Reuters news agency that officers fired tear gas at protesting inmates at an open prison in the coastal town of Negombo, about 40km (25 miles) from Colombo, to bring the situation there under control on Friday.

Riot police at all three prisons worked to return prisoners who had climbed onto rooftops or moved into open areas back to their wards, the minister said.

Wijepala told parliament the violence was related to narcotics dealers and rival criminal gangs.

He said the government is trying to find out if the riots were coordinated.

“When you take all ⁠these incidents together, it appears that there is planning behind these and an attempt at sabotage. But we can only say ⁠anything further after a comprehensive investigation,” Wijepala said.

The prison disturbances happened a month after 10 ⁠prison officials and 20 prisoners died in two days of fighting at a prison in Negombo.



One inmate also died and several others ‌were injured in a riot last weekend at a prison in Mahara, about 14km (8.6 miles) from Colombo.

Overcrowding in Sri Lanka’s prisons is at crisis levels.

Facilities are highly congested, with more than 39,000 inmates crowded into a system with a total capacity of just 10,000, according to a recent speech in parliament by Justice Minister Harshana Nanayakkara.

“The number of prisoners in Sri Lanka today is four times the capacity,” said Senaka Perera, president of the Committee for Rights of Prisoners. “In fact, they have been patient for so long.”

A large number of inmates are suspects awaiting trial for alleged narcotics-related offences. Recent laws tightening bail conditions have resulted in prison overcrowding, Perera said.

Sri Lanka is planning to amend its constitution ‌to extend superior court judges’ tenure by two years, as part of efforts to clear a backlog of more than one million court cases and reduce prisoner numbers.

World.title: Seized on Their Way to Gaza, Activists Tell of Abuse in Israeli Custody
World.content:
The stated goal of the activists, who sailed from Turkey on May 14, was to bring food and humanitarian aid to the war-ravaged enclave. In reality, many expected to be detained, like those who had participated in similar flotillas, before reaching the territory. They hoped that media coverage of their journey would call attention to Israel’s restrictions on supplies to Gaza, which tightened after the war began — and which later contributed, experts said, to famine in parts of Gaza.

The activists were captured days after setting sail. Interviews with activists and statements from Israeli officials both show that they were then held by Israel for roughly three days, first at sea aboard Israeli vessels, and later in the Port of Ashdod.

There, Israel’s national security minister, Itamar Ben-Gvir, walked among them, taunting them in a video he posted to social media. At least two of the activists were immediately deported to Greece, while the rest spent the night in prison in southern Israel before being deported to Turkey, they said.

After the detainees arrived in Turkey, the flotilla’s organizers soon announced that the detainees had made “numerous reports of physical abuse” as well as “deeply disturbing accounts of sexual humiliation and degrading treatment carried out by Israeli forces.”

More than 50 were brought by ambulance to hospitals from the airport in Turkey, according to a lawyer for the flotilla. Over the following days, activists began returning to their home countries, where they often sought more treatment and gave more detailed accounts of their detention to international news outlets. Their accusations spurred condemnations from global leaders and investigations by prosecutors in countries including France and Italy, and by police officers in Australia.

World.title: Foreigners Behaving Badly in Vietnam Challenge Its Communist Justice System
World.content:
He looked like one of the many digital nomads appearing in Vietnam these days as he plopped his bag on a table near the back of a stylish cafe and ordered a coffee.

Then he ripped off his shirt and ordered everyone to leave.

Security footage captured the man, Shaymus Lilly, 34, an Australian brand strategist, clearing counters and shattering windows at Gé Cafe in the coastal city of Da Nang. He smashed a stranger’s phone and choked a young Vietnamese man before police officers hauled him away.

World.title: Seven killed after Thai student opens fire at home and school
World.content:
At least seven people have been killed and 23 injured after a 14-year-old boy opened fire at his home and school on the outskirts of Thailand's capital, Bangkok.

The gunman - a student at the Debsirin School in Nonthaburi - killed his grandparents and five teachers before taking his own life, Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul told reporters. The attacker still had "more than 30 bullets left" when he turned the gun on himself, Anutin added.

Nine of the injured people remain in a critical condition, authorities say.

The shooting - the second at a school in Thailand this year - has renewed pressure on the government for greater action on gun control.

Police were deployed to the scene during the active shooting, which began just after 10:00 local time (03:00 GMT).

National police chief police Gen Kittiratt Phanphet told reporters that forensic officers had found the gunman's shots were quite accurate, with several hitting vital spots on the body.

The prime minister said the attack was "well prepared" with "clear steps and clear goals".

A female seventh grader, still in school uniform, told the BBC she was standing in front of her teacher when the woman was shot.

"She was talking to me when [the gunman] showed up and shot her," she said.

"I couldn't see anything but a [cloud] of dust."

Still in her uniform, with her mother by her side, she explained how the shooter stalked from room to room.

"I had to climb over the school fence to escape with other friends."

Her mother says the girl thought she might die. "[She said] 'I thought I'd never see you again'."

Another student told Reuters news agency that he had thought the sound of gunshots were firecrackers going off.

"There were many shots: bang bang bang. Then it went quiet. Then it started again."

Students and school staff were seen fleeing from the scene, and those waiting outside the Debsirin School looked visibly distraught.

Authorities warned people to stay away from the area and for those trapped in the building to hide and wait for rescuers.

In a post on social media, the school later shared a call for blood donations.

Other schools in the vicinity suspended classes so students could return home early.

World.title: Spain threatens retaliation if Italy fails to lift border controls after Ceuta crossings
World.content:
Spain has threatened to impose counter-measures on Italy if it fails to lift border controls introduced following the mass crossing of migrants into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta.

Roughly 78,000 migrants from neighbouring Morocco arrived in Ceuta by sea in a matter of hours on Thursday and Friday last week.

In the wake of the crossings, which saw around 100 people die, Italy partially suspended its Schengen arrangement with Spain, which included the closure of maritime and air entry points as well as the reinforcement of land border controls.

On Friday, Spain called the move "unjustified" and "discriminatory against the Spanish population" and demanded it be reversed by Sunday 9 August.

It added it would introduce "proportionate measures to protect the interests and dignity of its citizens" if Italy failed to reverse its decision.

The statement did not specify what these reprisals would be.

Italy promptly responded to Spain's warning, saying it would not accept "ultimatums or impositions" from Madrid and that it plans to keep border checks in place until at least 15 August - when it says Spain "expects a new wave of migration" to hit Ceuta.

Spain has not announced an anticipated second wave of crossings. Reports have been fuelled by social media activity by Moroccan users planning another attempt, El Pais reports.

The Spanish prime minister's office told the newspaper they were monitoring the situation but did not expect a repeat of scenes from last week.

World.title: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan sign defence pact
World.content:
Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan have signed a joint defence agreement, saying an attack on one of them would be seen as an attack on all three.

The pact was announced at a meeting between Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in the Saudi city of Mecca.

The three countries have been looking to strengthen security ties as the war between the US and Iran has drawn in Saudi Arabia and disrupted maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial oil shipping channel, and the Red Sea.

Saudi Arabia and Pakistan had already announced a joint defence pact last year.

The new Mecca Joint Defence Agreement sees three of the world's most powerful Muslim nations come together to offer mutual defence guarantees.

It aims "to strengthen collective deterrence against any act of aggression, and stipulates that any armed attack against any one of the three States shall be regarded as an attack against them all", a joint statement reads.

"It further provides for the enhancement of all aspects of defence co-operation among the three States."

Although the pact pledges mutual support, it provides no specifics on the obligations of each party. A Turkish official quoted by Reuters news agency said the pact was "purely defensive in nature".

Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey each bring different qualities to the table, with each wanting something different out of it.

For the Saudis, this gives an extra level of security in a region whose security architecture has been upended by the US and Israel's war with Iran.

After the US and Israel attacked Shia Islam-dominated Iran on 28 February, Tehran and its allies launched attacks on targets in Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states and blockaded their shipments - something that seemed unthinkable until recently.

Last month, Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels â who control much of the north-west of the country - announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and targeted Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.

World.title: Meta fined $567m in largest child safety ruling against social media giant
World.content:
A US judge in New Mexico has ordered Meta to pay another $567m (Â£421m) for its failure to warn the public about dangers its platforms posed to children, marking the largest fine against the company over child safety.

Judge Bryan Biedscheid said the social media giant is a "public nuisance" akin to air pollution and that it must put the money in a fund aimed at reducing future harms.

Thursday's ruling is in addition to $375m in fines Meta was already ordered to pay in the case, for a total of $942m.

Judge Biedscheid compared Meta to a factory, with advertising and content as its product and "the psychological harm and sexual exploitation of children to be the pollution that must be abated".

A spokesman for Meta, which owns and operates Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp and Threads, said Thursday: "We disagree with the ruling and will appeal."

"We work hard to keep people safe on our platforms and have been transparent about the challenges of identifying and removing bad actors and harmful content," they added.

"We remain confident in our record of protecting teens online and will continue to defend ourselves against claims that misrepresent the facts."

Regarding the earlier $375m verdict in the case, Meta had said it intended to appeal the ruling and gave a similar explanation. It was the first time that a state had successfully sued Meta over child safety issues.

Meta is currently facing thousands of lawsuits in the US over similar issues. In addition to the New Mexico rulings, Meta earlier this year lost a landmark case in Los Angeles which found it could be held liable for building addictive platforms.

Bruce Daisley, a former European vice president of Twitter (now X), told BBC Radio 4's Today programme the New Mexico fine, while large, was "a drop in the ocean" for Meta.

In its latest financial results, the social media giant posted $61bn in revenue from April to June - up 28% on the same period a year ago.

"But it's an indication that we are moving to a stage where social media is going to be tackled around the world," he said.

Meanwhile, former safeguarding minister Jess Phillips told Today she believed US court challenges against big tech could enable the UK to take tougher action - without fearing it may damage UK-US diplomatic ties.

World.title: Spanish police arrest 78 people in bust of 'one of largest' smuggling networks
World.content:
One of the largest criminal networks smuggling drugs and people in the western Mediterranean has been dismantled, authorities have said.

Europol said 78 people were arrested in Spain and Algeria in a bust of the network, that is also linked to other criminal activities including "violent robberies, extortion, illegal detentions, and money laundering".

The group moved synthetic drugs from Spain and Portugal to Algeria, then used the return journey to smuggle migrants and weapons to the Spanish mainland and island of Ibiza on "ghost speedboats".

Some of the items seized included 18 high-speed vessels valued at â¬5m (Â£4.2m), guns, more than â¬25,000 (Â£21,400) in cash and 15,000 MDMA pills.

The sting, led by Spanish police, involved searches in 17 locations in Spain, including Alicante, AlmerÃ­a, Cartagena and Murcia.

Europol said the group had "evolved from drug trafficking into a duel-flow criminal enterprise designed to maximise profits" with outbound routes from Spain and Portugal to Algeria.

"The smuggling focused on synthetic drugs (such as MDMA), firearms, and explosives. Along routine routes from Algeria to Spain, the group smuggled migrants, charging up to â¬12,000 (Â£10,200) per person," Europol's statement said.

"In just one trip, over 50 migrants could be smuggled. All in all, profits from migrant smuggling alone are estimated to be more than â¬24m (Â£20m)."

The network also provided services to other organised crime groups, "facilitating the movement of illicit goods and people across the Western Mediterranean".

"Investigators believe the network coordinated multiple trafficking flows. Synthetic drugs, and sometimes people, were moved from France and Spain to Algeria, while cannabis resin, weapons, and migrants were transported from Algeria to Spain."

Often, the group used a fleet of high-powered speedboats to conduct rapid maritime operations. This included "ghost speedboats" which are designed to avoid registration and detection, which are prohibited in Spain.

"The group used these boats to organise transfers in international waters near the Spanish coastline," Europol said. "Once the cargo or migrants were handed over at sea, other network members arranged onward transport by land.

"Migrants were often carried in overcrowded boats without lighting or life jackets, frequently under extreme weather conditions.

"Investigators believe suspects perpetrated sexual assaults, physical abuse, and placed migrants in inhuman conditions in makeshift housing."

The suspects were primarily of Algerian origin and had connections to criminal groups in France, Belgium, Portugal, Italy and Poland.

Other objects seized in the police sting included satellite phones, GPS devices, encrypted communication tools and satellite dishes.

The announcement comes a week after roughly 78,000 migrants fled into the Spanish North African territory of Ceuta that was blamed on online rumours about an open border.

Most of the migrants returned to Morocco but between 3,000 and 5,000 remain in the territory, the exclave's leader Juan JesÃºs Vivas said.

World.title: Mexico and Peru restore diplomatic relations after asylum row
World.content:
Mexico and Peru have agreed to re-establish diplomatic relations following a row over the granting of asylum to a former Peruvian prime minister who was charged for a 2022 coup attempt.

In a joint statement released on 7 August, Lima and Mexico City said "historic ties of brotherhood, friendship and cooperation" prompted the reconciliation.

The two countries also reaffirmed "their respect for international law and the principles of the Charter of the United Nations".

Relations broke down after former Peruvian Prime Minister Betssy ChÃ¡vez sought asylum in the Mexican embassy in November 2025.

World.title: Trump again tries to limit US birthright citizenship with new executive orders
World.content:
Donald Trump is trying again to scale back birthright citizenship in the US, weeks after the Supreme Court shot down his previous attempt to eliminate the right.

The president signed two executive orders on Thursday, including one that expands the existing definitions of non-citizens whose children are not eligible for birthright citizenship.

The second order bans so-called birth tourism, the practice of pregnant mothers coming to the US to give birth so that their babies will be citizens.

"This should have happened years ago, but we're taking care of it now," Trump said from the Oval Office, criticising the Supreme Court's rejection of his previous bid to end the 150-year-old policy.

"My Administration has guarded against the risks posed by malign foreign actors who attempt to swindle American citizens by taking advantage of the generosity of our Nation," the first executive order says.

That order prohibits the automatic citizenship of babies born in the United States to two non-citizen parents where one of the parents is: a member of a foreign terrorist group, a foreign government employee, has attempted to gain citizenship through fraudulent means, or is living in US territories where citizenship is not conferred by federal statute.

Birthright citizenship for people born in US territories such as Puerto Rico is codified by federal statute.

Trump and members of his administration have repeatedly railed against birth tourism, including accusing Russian and Chinese adversaries of taking advantage of birthright citizenship to infiltrate the US.

While announcing the executive orders from the Oval Office on Thursday, Trump said that hundreds of thousands of babies have been born through birth tourism in the US.

World.title: A new youth agitation grips an Indian state after 'cockroach' protests
World.content:
Weeks after thousands of young Indians poured onto the streets of Delhi in a major 'cockroach' protest over examination paper leaks, another group of frustrated job seekers is making headlines - this time hundreds of miles away, in the eastern state of Jharkhand.

Protesters have gathered at a stadium in the state capital Ranchi, since 25 July, demanding an overhaul of the state's government examination system. Some have been sleeping in the open and several have gone on hunger strike.

Umme Habiba is one of them.

The 27-year-old, from a farming family from Bokaro, has spent years preparing for Jharkhand's civil service examination, hoping it would get her the security of a government job. She has already sat the exam three times and hoped to get a good score this time.

"We want justice. We will not leave until we get it, even if it costs us our lives," she said.

The immediate cause of the anger is a preliminary civil service examination held in April.

After the results were announced in July, candidates alleged that leaked answer sheets shared on social media showed some successful applicants had answered far fewer questions than expected.

This fuelled suspicions that the results had been manipulated. The protesters want the exam scrapped and held again. They also want the case investigated by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), India's premier federal investigative agency.

The allegations are being investigated by Jharkhand's Criminal Investigation Department (CID) and the Jharkhand Public Service Commission has since postponed the next stage of the examination. Its chairman, L Khiangte, resigned on 22 July and has been questioned as part of the investigation.

Investigators are also examining the role of a private company that conducted parts of the examination process, after candidates raised questions about how it was selected.

Deepika Pandey Singh, a minister in the Jharkhand government, told the BBC that the state had begun investigating the allegations even before the current protest.

She urged protesters to let the CID complete its investigation instead of handing the case to the CBI. "We want a fair investigation," she said, adding that anyone responsible - "whether a bureaucrat, employee, middleman or a big politician" - would face action. She also said the government would discuss the protesters' demand to cancel the April exam with them directly.

World.title: IGP explains appointment of CP for Osun governorship election
World.content:
The Inspector-General of Police, Tunji Disu, on Friday said the Nigeria Police Force appointed Samuel Erale as the Commissioner of Police (CP) in charge of security during the forthcoming 15 August governorship election to restore confidence in the command’s neutrality.

Mr Disu said the subtantive CP, Ibrahim Gotan, was asked to step aside after political parties raised concerns about the neutrality of the Osun State Police Command, stressing that the decision was not a disciplinary action against him.

The Whistler reported that the IGP disclosed this on Friday in Abuja during a meeting with civil society organisations on election security in Osun State, led by the Executive Director of YIAGA Africa, Samson Itodo.

He said the police took the decision as a confidence-building measure to reassure political parties and other stakeholders that the force would remain neutral before, during and after the election.

The IGP said the decision followed rising political tension and violence in the state, with police intelligence linking some of the unrest to rival cult groups allegedly associated with political actors.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Certain groups of politicians or parties have been complaining that they no longer trust the Commissioner of Police. So the Commissioner of Police was asked to stand aside, while the Electoral Commissioner of Police took over,” Mr Disu said.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that Mr Erale, the Electoral Commissioner of Police, had consequently assumed responsibility for election security in the state, while the Assistant Inspector-General of Police in charge of elections is expected to join the operation.

The development also follows weeks of political controversy over the conduct of the police command, including allegations of partisanship by political parties and civil society groups.

The Accord Party had demanded the removal of Mr Gotan, while civil society organisations also protested in Osogbo over what they described as concerns about the neutrality of the police ahead of the election.

The controversy intensified after the arrest of the Secretary to the Osun State Government, Teslim Igbalaye, and others during a police operation at his residence over alleged electoral offences.

The state government and supporters of Governor Ademola Adeleke criticised the operation, describing it as politically motivated, while the police maintained that it was part of an investigation. Mr Igbalaye was subsequently released.

However, barely 24 hours after Mr Igbalaye’s release, the Command announced the deployment of Mr Erale to oversee the state election and security of the state.

Against this backdrop, Mr Disu said the decision to replace the commissioner was intended to prevent the controversy surrounding the command from undermining confidence in the electoral process.

Concerns of partisanship of federal agencies regarding deepened on Wednesday when the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) blocked an Osun State Government account domiciled at First Bank.

In response to public outrage about the development, President Bola Tinubu, whose party, the All Progressives Congress, is fielding a candidate, Bola Oyebamiji, against Governor Ademola Adeleke of the Accord Party in the forthcoming governorship election, intervened on Thursday, ordering the EFCC to lift the freeze order on the state’s account.

World.title: Osun Election: IGP assures voters of adequate security as Yiaga identifies 13 high-risk LGAs
World.content:
The Inspector-General of Police (IGP), Olatunji Disu, has assured residents of Osun State of adequate security ahead of the forthcoming governorship election, saying the force has put in place extensive measures to protect voters, electoral officials and other stakeholders throughout the electoral process.

Mr Disu gave the assurance on Friday during a stakeholders’ engagement on election security with civil society organisations, amid growing concerns over rising political violence in the state.

Also, a civil society organisation, Yiaga Africa, identified 13 of the state’s 30 local government areas as high-risk locations, citing persistent attacks, political tension and at least 34 deaths linked to election-related violence recorded over the past year.

During the meeting, the IGP urged eligible voters not to be intimidated by security concerns but to come out in large numbers to exercise their constitutional right to vote.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said the police would provide security before, during and after the election to ensure a peaceful and credible process.

“We want the people of Osun State to come out and vote without fear. The Nigeria Police Force is fully prepared to secure the election and ensure that every eligible voter can exercise their democratic rights safely,” he said.

Police deploy officers to over 3,000 polling units

The police chief disclosed that security personnel would be deployed across more than 3,000 polling units in the state, with at least four officers assigned to each.

He added that additional security arrangements had been put in place to respond swiftly to any security threats that might arise during the election.

Mr Disu also revealed that an Assistant Inspector-General of Police would soon relocate to Osun to coordinate election security, strengthening the existing command structure ahead of the poll.

He explained that the police had already made strategic changes in the state’s security leadership after violence escalated.

According to him, the former Commissioner of Police in Osun was directed to step aside to allow another officer to oversee election security operations.

The IGP attributed much of the violence in the state to pre-existing cult-related rivalries that had become intertwined with political competition.

“We have issues of cultism in Osun already. It became easier for different parties to attack each other using the existing animosity in the state,” he said.

Mr Disu stressed that no political ambition was worth the loss of lives.

“No election is worthy of losing anyone because elections will come and go,” he said, while appealing to political parties, candidates and their supporters to conduct their campaigns peacefully and respect the rule of law.

Yiaga warns of insecurity, identifies flashpoints

Earlier, the Executive Director of Yiaga Africa, Samson Itodo, described the Osun governorship election as one of the most significant off-cycle elections in recent years because it would be the last major governorship election before the 2027 general elections.

He said the poll presents an opportunity to rebuild public confidence not only in Nigeria’s electoral management system but also in election security.

“The Osun election is strategically important because it is the last major election before the 2027 general elections. It is a unique opportunity to inspire public trust, not just in the management of elections, but also in election security,” he said.

Mr Itodo warned that insecurity and any perception of bias by security agencies could undermine the credibility of the election and weaken public confidence in democratic institutions.

According to him, Yiaga Africa’s election risk assessment identified 13 local government areas as high-risk due to recurring killings, violent attacks and heightened political tension.

He said the pattern of violence had evolved from coordinated shootings across several communities to politically motivated abductions and attacks on public institutions, including local government secretariats.

The organisation’s monitoring, he said, recorded about 44 violent incidents between June 2025 and June 2026, resulting in approximately 34 deaths.

Among the identified hotspots, Osogbo and Irewole LGAs were categorised as critical-risk areas, while Iwo, Boripe, Ife Central and Ife East LGAs were listed as high-risk local government areas requiring an enhanced security presence.

Mr Itodo said one of the greatest concerns expressed by citizens was the perceived neutrality of security agencies during elections.

He urged the police and other security agencies to remain professional and resist any attempt by political actors to influence their operations.

“The public wants to see institutions demonstrate neutrality so they can have confidence in the electoral process. An election marred by insecurity or perceived security bias could undermine public trust and the legitimacy of the outcome,” he said.

CISLAC calls for impartial policing

Also speaking, the Executive Director of the Civil Society Legislative Advocacy Centre (CISLAC) and Head of Transparency International Nigeria, Auwal Rafsanjani, pledged the support of civil society organisations for security agencies in ensuring peaceful elections.

He said civil society groups were not opponents of government, but partners committed to strengthening Nigeria’s democracy.

According to him, political tension ahead of the 2027 general elections makes it imperative for security agencies to act professionally and impartially.

“The safety and security of Nigerians during elections is extremely important. Our role as civil society is to support the security agencies so they can perform their responsibilities without bias or actions capable of eroding public confidence,” he said.

Mr Rafsanjani expressed confidence in the leadership of the IGP, saying his record would help guarantee credible election security.

He added that civil society organisations had developed recommendations to promote peaceful, violence-free, and internationally credible elections, stressing the need for continued collaboration between security agencies and non-state actors to safeguard Nigeria’s democracy.

The Osun governorship election is scheduled to hold on Saturday, 15 August, when eligible voters across the state’s 30 local government areas will elect a governor for a fresh four-year term.

The election is one of Nigeria’s off-cycle governorship polls, held outside the general election calendar due to judicial decisions that altered the tenures of previous administrations.

It is also regarded as the final major standalone election before the 2027 general elections, making it an important test of the country’s electoral and security institutions.

The contest is expected to be keenly fought, with incumbent Governor Ademola Adeleke of the Accord Party seeking re-election after leaving the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP).

His main challenger is Bola Oyebamiji (AMBO) of the All Progressives Congress (APC), while Najeem Salaam is contesting on the platform of the African Democratic Congress (ADC).

World.title: Lawmakers seek emergency parliamentary session over insecurity, budget implementation
World.content:
Some serving members of the House of Representatives, operating under the banner of the Save Democracy Group (SDG), have warned that Nigeria’s democracy is facing a dangerous decline, citing alleged constitutional violations, chronic budget under-implementation, opaque public spending, worsening insecurity and growing economic hardship.

In a statement dated 5 August and signed by the group’s leader, Awaji-Inombek Abiante (PDP, Rivers), alongside Abubakar Kusada (APC, Katsina) and Mansur Jega (ADC, Kebbi), the lawmakers called on the leadership of the National Assembly to immediately reconvene both chambers from recess to address what they described as urgent constitutional, fiscal and security concerns.

SDG described itself as a non-partisan platform of members of the 10th National Assembly committed to defending democracy, constitutional governance, legislative independence, accountability and the rule of law.

It stressed that its members cut across political parties and regions and insisted that it was neither an opposition platform nor a political pressure group.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Our membership cuts across political parties, regions and ideological differences. We are neither an opposition platform nor an instrument of any political interest. We are legislators increasingly alarmed by the direction of Nigeria’s democracy,” the statement said.

Questions over constitutional procedures

The lawmakers accused public institutions of increasingly treating constitutional provisions as optional and warned that such practices threaten democratic governance.

They revisited the National Assembly’s approval of the declaration of a state of emergency in Rivers State in March 2025, arguing that the reliance on a voice vote was inconsistent with Section 305(6) of the Constitution, which requires approval by a two-thirds majority of all members of each chamber.

The group also questioned the House’s passage of the Executive State Police Constitutional Alteration Bill on 23 July 2026.

According to the statement, although Speaker Abbas Tajudeen announced that 311 lawmakers voted in favour of the bill, some members present throughout the proceedings maintained that fewer than the constitutionally required 240 members were physically present in the chamber.

The group alleged that the announced figure could only have been achieved by counting votes transmitted through WhatsApp by members who were not physically present during the proceedings.

It argued that Section 9(2) of the Constitution requires the affirmative votes of not less than two-thirds of all members before any constitutional amendment can be validly passed.

“The Constitution cannot be altered by presumption, improvisation or undisclosed voting arrangements,” the lawmakers said.

While acknowledging that state police may be a desirable reform, they insisted that constitutional amendments establishing it must strictly comply with constitutional procedures.

Budget implementation under scrutiny

The lawmakers also expressed concern over what they described as persistent failures by the federal government to fully implement annual budgets.

They argued that the repeated extensions of budget implementation periods and the rollover of capital projects from one fiscal year to the next had weakened fiscal discipline and legislative oversight.

According to the statement, only about 30 per cent of the 2025 capital budget was reportedly funded, with approximately 70 per cent carried over into 2026.

The group cited remarks previously made by Senate Chief Whip Tahir Monguno, who reportedly described the failure to implement an Appropriation Act as a breach of the law that could amount to an impeachable offence.

The lawmakers endorsed that position, arguing that deliberate or persistent refusal to implement duly enacted Appropriation Acts raises serious constitutional issues.

They demanded comprehensive implementation reports for the 2024, 2025 and 2026 budgets; full disclosure of capital releases to ministries, departments and agencies; reconciliation of revenues with authorised expenditure; explanations for delayed capital releases; a joint parliamentary investigation into budget implementation failures; and constitutional action where deliberate non-implementation is established.

“An Appropriation Act is law, and the government cannot choose which laws to obey,” they stated.

Concern over alleged off-budget spending

The group further called for an independent forensic audit into reports of alleged off-budget public expenditure.

It referred to reports that the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated that public expenditure equivalent to about two per cent of Nigeria’s Gross Domestic Product, approximately ₦8.83 trillion, was not reflected in recent official budgets.

According to the lawmakers, if confirmed, such expenditure would represent a significant discrepancy between Nigeria’s declared fiscal deficit and its actual financing requirements.

They argued that allegations of unrecorded public spending warrant immediate legislative scrutiny and insisted that public funds must not be spent outside duly approved Appropriation Acts.

“This administration cannot demand sacrifice from Nigerians while public expenditure remains opaque,” the statement said.

The lawmakers maintained that every naira spent by the government belongs to Nigerians and must be fully accounted for through transparent appropriation and expenditure processes.

Security funding concerns

On insecurity, the group said the continued killings, kidnappings and displacement of citizens by terrorists, bandits and other criminal groups remained unacceptable.

The lawmakers also cited reports indicating that some security agencies had yet to receive capital releases despite the country’s worsening security situation.

They questioned what they described as disparities in government spending priorities, claiming that almost the entire allocation for the Presidential Air Fleet had reportedly been released, while only a small portion of funds appropriated for the Nigerian Army’s security equipment had been made available.

The lawmakers clarified that they were not opposed to maintaining the Presidential Air Fleet but argued that operational funding for security agencies should receive greater priority.

They therefore urged the immediate release of appropriated capital funds to the armed forces, the Nigeria Police Force, intelligence agencies and other security institutions.

Religious leaders commended

The group commended the Catholic Bishops’ Conference of Nigeria (CBCN) for publicly raising concerns over insecurity, economic hardship and democratic decline.

It also praised the Supreme Council for Shari’ah in Nigeria for urging wider consultations and caution over the proposed establishment of state police.

According to the lawmakers, both religious bodies demonstrated patriotism by speaking on national issues and emphasising constitutional safeguards.

Call for emergency parliamentary session

The lawmakers urged the President of the Senate and the Speaker of the House of Representatives to immediately reconvene both chambers to deliberate on what they described as pressing national issues.

They said the emergency session should focus on the under-implementation of the 2024, 2025 and 2026 budgets, the constitutional controversy surrounding the State Police Constitutional Alteration Bill, allegations of off-budget expenditure, the non-release of capital funds to security agencies, the country’s worsening security situation and measures to restore public confidence in democratic governance.

“The National Assembly is not merely an institution for passing Executive Bills and approving requests from the Presidency. It is an independent arm of government constitutionally empowered to represent the people, defend the Constitution, appropriate public funds, conduct oversight and hold the Executive accountable,” the statement said.

The group maintained that it was not opposed to state police, economic reforms, or necessary public expenditure, but insisted that constitutional procedures, transparent budgeting, and accountability must not be sacrificed.

It warned that history would judge members of the 10th National Assembly by whether they defended the Constitution and protected the interests of Nigerians during what it described as a defining moment for the country’s democracy.

World.title: Atiku raises alarm over suspicious credit alert in his bank account
World.content:
Former Vice President and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has raised the alarm over a suspicious credit into one of his private bank accounts domiciled with one of Nigeria’s leading commercial banks.

This was contained in a statement by his Senior Special Assistant on Public Communication, Phrank Shaibu, on Friday in Abuja.

According to the statement, the transfer, with the narration “Contribution Electioneering Campaign,” originated from a person totally unknown to the former vice president.

“Neither His Excellency nor his campaign solicited, authorised or has any knowledge of the individual or entity behind the unauthorised payment,” it said, adding that the circumstances surrounding the transfer are deeply troubling to him.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Read the full statement

MYSTERIOUS CREDIT: ATIKU RAISES ALARM OVER SUSPECTED LEAK OF PRIVATE BANK DETAILS

Former Vice President of Nigeria and Presidential Candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has raised an alarm over a suspicious credit into one of his private bank accounts domiciled with one of Nigeria’s leading commercial banks.

The transfer originated from a person totally unknown to His Excellency, with the narration “Contribution Electioneering Campaign.” Neither His Excellency nor his campaign solicited, authorised or has any knowledge of the individual or entity behind the unauthorised payment.

Understandably, the circumstances surrounding the transfer are deeply troubling to His Excellency. The account is a strictly private one whose details are not in the public domain. This raises a fundamental question: How did unknown persons obtain the confidential banking details of a private citizen?

If the private banking information of a former Vice President and a leading presidential candidate can be accessed and deployed for reasons yet unknown, then no Nigerian’s financial privacy is safe. Even more disturbing is the suspicion that such confidential information may have been obtained through persons with privileged access. If established, this would amount to a grave abuse of power capable of exposing the account holder to kidnappers, terrorists, bandits, fraudsters and other criminal elements.

We therefore put the Nigerian public – and the security agencies – on notice about this latest incident in a litany of suspicious activities leading up to next year’s general elections.

As political activities gather momentum, Nigerians should not be distracted by these tired tactics that smack of character assassination. Such desperate antics have failed before and will fail again. The Waziri Adamawa remains focused on offering Nigerians credible leadership and practical solutions to the nation’s challenges.

Signed:

Phrank Shaibu

Senior Special Assistant on Public Communication to Atiku Abubakar, Vice President of Nigeria (1999–2007) and Presidential Candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC).

7th August, 2026

World.title: ACAMB holds Golf and Networking Experience to mark 30th anniversary
World.content:
As part of activities lined up to commemorate its 30th anniversary, Association of Corporate Communication and Marketing Professionals in Banks (ACAMB) recently hosted a Golf and Networking Experience with senior executives of banks, captains of industry, Media partners and clients in attendance.

Held at the prestigious Ikoyi Club 1938, the networking initiative designed to promote unity, genuine connections and partnerships was organised to honour three decades of advancing corporate communications and marketing excellence within the nation’s banking industry.

ACAMB President, Jide Sipe, who welcomed members and dignitaries to the networking event, reaffirmed the Association’s commitment to the reputation and growth of the banking industry.

“Over the past 30 years marketing and corporate communications professionals have continued to contribute significantly to the transformation of the financial sector from a closed-door industry into an ecosystem driven by transparency, speed, and digital engagement. We have remained consistent, from gatekeepers to strategic drivers in actualising growth, positive brand perception, aligning business values to customer needs, customer satisfaction and loyalty. The list is endless.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Sipe further noted that, marketing professionals continue to hold sway in driving a core strategic function that directly impacts market valuation and regulatory compliance coupled with Information democratization, reputation management as well as education of the public sector on complex monetary policies.

“All this have to great extent catalysed the growth trajectory of the financial sector and to that, we feel a sense of pride, worthy of celebration, that is why, we picked a partner, with great pedigree like Ikoyi Club 1938, for this purpose. We have all come out today to play golf, celebrate, unwind, network as well as discuss new and innovative ways that will further see us soar together”.

Mr Sipe also used the opportunity to commend the club for its longstanding legacy of community building, family bonding, and excellence in sports development within Nigeria, which continues to help nurture the social fabric of businesses. This he said is a strong alignment with social growth.

The Deputy Chairman of Ikoyi Club 1938, Mr Bolaji Martins, congratulated ACAMB on its upcoming anniversary in September and thanked ACAMB’s president for choosing the club for the auspicious occasion.

I know where the sector was 30 years before now and cannot but appreciate the giant leap it has attained, thanks to the yeoman effort of this impressive association”

“Having said that, we are committing to giving opportunity at a discounted rate to members of ACAMB and interested professionals who are interested in joining our club as a form of appreciation and support, considering the good work they continue to do, Mr Martins said.

World.title: NAFDAC warns of suspected counterfeit asthma medication found in Nigerian market
World.content:
The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has alerted Nigerians to the circulation of a suspected counterfeit asthma medicine, warning that its use could lead to treatment failure and other serious health risks.

The agency made this known on Friday in a public alert shared on its official X account, saying the suspected falsified product, Ulmicort 0.5 mg/ml Inhalation Suspension, was detected during market surveillance conducted by pharmaceutical company AstraZeneca.

According to NAFDAC, AstraZeneca informed the agency that the product closely resembles its registered asthma medicine, Pulmicort (Budesonide) Nebulising Suspension, and could mislead healthcare professionals and patients.

Pulmicort is an inhaled corticosteroid prescribed to prevent asthma symptoms such as wheezing and shortness of breath, and is used as a maintenance treatment for people living with asthma.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Health risks

NAFDAC warned that counterfeit medicines may not meet the required standards of quality, safety and efficacy.

It explained that such products could contain incorrect ingredients, the wrong quantity of active ingredients, harmful contaminants, or no active ingredient at all.

“The use of such products can result in treatment failure, worsening of respiratory conditions, unexpected adverse effects and other serious health consequences,” the agency said.

Asthma is a chronic disease that affects the airways in the lungs, causing them to become inflamed and narrowed. It can lead to symptoms such as wheezing, coughing, chest tightness and difficulty breathing, and requires regular treatment to keep symptoms under control.

Product traced to Anambra

Providing details of the suspected counterfeit product, NAFDAC said it bears the batch number 25770416E, with a manufacturing date of June 2025 and an expiry date of May 2027.

It was reportedly found in Eastern Nigeria and traced to a distributor’s address at 15 Chizzon, Awada, Obosi North, Anambra State.

The agency added that the suspected counterfeit product is labelled as being manufactured by Legency Remedies PVT Ltd, located in Himachal Pradesh, India.

NAFDAC said it has commenced an investigation to determine the source and distribution network of the suspected counterfeit medicine.

The agency added that all its zonal directors and state coordinators have been directed to intensify surveillance and conduct mop-up operations to remove the product from circulation nationwide.

READ ALSO: NAFDAC blacklists Onifam Laboratories over regulatory violations

Advice to consumers

NAFDAC urged consumers and healthcare professionals to buy medicines only from licensed pharmacies and authorised distributors, and to examine product labels and packaging before use carefully.

The agency also encouraged the public to report suspected cases of counterfeit or substandard medicines to the nearest NAFDAC office via its toll-free line, email, or online reporting platforms.

It advised healthcare professionals and patients to promptly report any adverse reactions linked to medicinal products through its pharmacovigilance reporting channels.

World.title: Friday Sermon: Beware, the flesh of Islamic scholars (Ulama’) is poisonous!, By Murtadha Gusau
World.content:
In the name of Allah, Most Merciful, the Bestower of Mercy

All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds and Lord of all creation — may the salutations of Allah, His peace and blessings be upon the noblest of all of the Prophets and Messengers, Muhammad, upon his family, his Companions and all those who follow them precisely until the establishment of the Hour.

Dear brothers and sisters! Know that, the famous statement “The flesh of Islamic scholars is poisonous” is a famous maxim coined by the classical historian and great Islamic scholar, the author of a great, famous and popular book, ‘Tarikh Madinat Dimashq’ (The History of Damascus), Al-Hafiz, Imam Abul-Qasim Ali Ibn al-Hasan Ibn Asakir, and echoed by other notable Imams like Imam Ahmad Ibn Hanbal, to warn the Ummah against the grave spiritual danger of insulting, abusing, slandering, mocking, or unjustly attacking the honour of those who carry and teach the divine knowledge; the Ulama’.

Al-Hafiz, Imam Abul-Qasim Ali Ibn al-Hasan Ibn Asakir wrote in his book Tabyin Kazib al-Muftari:

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Know, O my brother—may Allah guide us and you—that the flesh of the Islamic scholars is poisonous, and Allah’s custom in exposing and destroying those who belittle them is well known.”

He added that:

“Whoever lets their tongue loose against the Islamic scholars with slander will be afflicted by Allah with the death of the heart, spiritual numbness and ruin, before they even die physically.”

No doubt, Islamic scholars are not infallible, but because they preserve and transmit the legacy and teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (Peace be upon him), attacking them is a direct assault on Islam and the vehicle of guidance itself.

Consuming the “flesh” of a person via backbiting is already a major sin likened in the noble Qur’an to eating the dead flesh of one’s brother. When the person slandered is a sincere guide of the religion, the spiritual toxicity and punishment are multiplied. Allah Almighty steps in to defend those who truly believe and guide others; those who make a habit of finding faults in or fabricating lies against the Islamic scholars and the people of knowledge invariably end up humiliated or spiritually bankrupt.

Unjustly tearing down Islamic scholars creates fitnah, discord, and blinds ordinary people from seeking authentic religious guidance, and fractures the unity and peace of the Muslim Ummah.

Islam teaches respect for the Islamic scholars and Ulama’ while acknowledging that they are human beings who can make mistakes. And remember, correcting or differing with an Islamic scholar based on solid textual evidence with proper respect is acceptable, but malicious character assassination, mockery, and cheap point-scoring on social media or from the religious or political pulpit destroy the critic’s own Hereafter.

Respected brothers and sisters! In a time when the status, rank and honour of the Islamic scholars are being maligned and attacked by some misguided political singers, or some ignorant politicians, or some callers to misguidance, it is must and appropriate that we make mention of some important narrations and scholarly sayings regarding this crucial subject. One should be in no doubt that those who revile, speak ill and belittle the Islamic scholars and put doubt in the hearts of the Muslims regarding them are criminals and misguided people.

This present band of misguided people openly declare particular Islamic scholars to be “driven by desires” whilst at the same time, “not caring” about the plight of Muslim Ummah.

Muslim Ummah should not be deceived by these plots, plans and schemes to turn people away from the Islamic knowledge.

Imam Ibn Majah reported in his Sunan that:

Amr Bin Shuʿaib narrated that his father said: Muʿawiyyah (RA) stood up to deliver a sermon and he said, “Where are your scholars? Where are your scholars? For I heard the Messenger of Allah (Peace be upon him) say: The Hour will not be established until a group of my Ummah is manifest over the people, and they do not care who lets them down, who betrays them or who supports them.” [See As-Sahihah of Shaikh al-Albani, Hadith no. 1165, 1958, 1971]

Due to the steadfastness of the Islamic scholars and their fear of Allah, they are not scared of the blame of blamers or the accusations of the ignorant people against them. They do not care if they are betrayed, opposed or abandoned. They are the followers and the inheritors of the Prophets, and they know that those who are tried and afflicted the most are the Prophets and Messengers of Allah, then those who resemble them. So they remain firm upon the Truth regardless of the opposition, even when the followers of truth are few in number.

Abdullah Ibn Masʿud (RA) explained:

“There will not come upon you a day except that it is worse than the day that came before it until the Hour is established. I do not mean in terms of affluence in one’s life or the wealth that one acquires. Rather, there will not come upon you a day except that it will be lesser in knowledge than the day that passed before it. So when the Islamic scholars have passed away and died, the people will all be at the same level – so they will not enjoin the good, nor forbid the evil, and at that point, they will be ruined.” [Reported by Imam Ad-Darimi and Ibn Hajr declared the narration to be good in Fathul-Bari, volume 13, page 26-27]

Abdullah Ibn Amr Ibn Al-As said: I heard Allah’s Messenger (Peace be upon him) saying:

“Allah does not take away the knowledge by taking it away from the hearts of the people, but He takes it away by the death of the Islamic scholars till no Islamic scholar remains. Then people will take as their leaders the ignoramuses who when asked will give their verdict (fatwa) without knowledge. So they will go astray themselves and will lead the people astray.” [Reported by Al-Bukhari]

In another wording, he said:

“There will remain the ignoramuses from whom verdicts (fatwas) will be sought. They will give verdicts based upon their own opinions, so they will go astray and will lead the people astray.” [Al-Bukhari]

When the Islamic scholars are abandoned or they pass away, people turn to the ignorant ones as their leaders, the pretenders, who lead the people into ruin.

Abdullah Ibn Masʿud said:

“Learn knowledge before it is taken away, and it is taken away by the death of the Islamic scholars. And beware of going to extremes and delving too deeply, and beware of innovations. Upon you is to adhere to the ancient affair.” [See Ad-Darimi with the explanation, Fathul-Mannan, volume 2, page 115, Al-Musannaf of Abdur-Razzaq, volume 11, page 252, Jami’u Bayan Al-Ilm wa Fadlihi, volume 1, page 152, and Al-Amr bil-Ittiba, page 59]

When the Islamic scholars are present, knowledge, action and piety are widespread. When the Islamic scholars are few and abandoned, and the riff-raff and rabble speak, knowledge diminishes along with deeds and piety. Abu Zar narrated from Allah’s Messenger (Peace be upon him):

“You are today in a time of many Islamic Scholars and few speakers. So whoever abandons even a tenth of what he knows is ruined. There will come after that a time of many ignorant speakers wherein the Islamic scholars are few. So whoever holds fast to even a tenth of what he knows will be saved.” [Reported by At-Tirmidhi, Ahmad in Al-Musnad, Al-Bukharī in At-Tarikh, Al-Harawi in Zammul-Kalam, and authenticated by Al-Albanī in As-Sahihah, Hadith no. 2510]

So when there are numerous speakers, musicians, content creators, mostly young, ignorant and reckless, who revile the Islamic scholars and belittle their worth; accusing them of being ignorant of current affairs and the reality of Muslim communities and societies, such that the people no longer distinguish between a person of knowledge and the riff-raff who call to misguidance, it is then that they are ruined.

In these times, this negativity towards the Islamic scholars is rampant and widespread – and these ignoramuses, who falsely ascribe themselves to Islam and Muslims wallahi are more harmful to the Islam and Muslims than the unbelievers.

Ash-Shaikh Rabīʿ Ibn Hadī Umair Al-Madkhali (rahimahullah) was asked regarding those who revile the Islamic scholars, so he answered:

“This is a very dangerous matter indeed, meaning: criticising those who are upon the Truth – attacking them leads to attacking and contending with the religion itself because it prevents people from the Path of Allah. That is due to the fact that the one who attacks the callers to the Truth, the callers to Tawhid, those who call to fight against shirk, bidʿah and misguidance – attacking them causes one to flee from the Path of Allah Almighty. And you know already what Allah has stated regarding those who opposed and attacked the Prophets. They would attack their callers, not so much their individuals. They would say: “He’s a liar, a magician..” and so on from terms of abuse. So if he is reviled in his character, then his Da’awah is lost. And this is the case today. The Islamic scholars are the inheritors of the Prophets. So when a people call to the Islam, to the Book of Allah, to the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (Peace be upon him), to the Methodology of the Prophets in Aqīdah, to fighting against shirk, upon the Methodology of the Prophets, then there come a people in opposition reviling them – and this means that they prevent people from the Path of Allah. So we ask Allah that He guides them to repent, and that they return to the Truth, that they recognise the position of the People of Truth, and they abandon their stance in front of those who are eager for the Truth so they do not prevent them from the Path of Allah.” [See Wujub Al-Ittibaʿ la Ibtida’ from the Shaikh’s website]

The role of the Islamic scholars is crucial in the preservation of the Religion of Allah. Allah’s Messenger (Peace be upon him) stated:

“This knowledge will be carried by the trustworthy of every generation. They will expel from it the distortions of those who go to extremes, the lies of the falsifiers, and the interpretations of the ignorant.” [Reported by Al-Baihaqī in As-Sunan Al-Kubra, At-Tabrīzī in Mishkat Al-Masabīh and Ibn Abdul-Barr in At-Tamhīd, volume 1, page 59]

So to attack the Islamic scholars is to harm those whom Allah has raised to preserve and guard His Religion against the people of falsehood and desires, and to block people from the Path of Allah.

As mentioned above, Al-Hafiz, Imam Abul-Qasim Ali Ibn al-Hasan Ibn Asakir (rahimahullah) said:

“Know, my brother – may Allah guide us and you to His pleasure, and that He makes us from those who fear Him and are dutiful to Him as He deserves – that the flesh of the Islamic scholars, may Allah be merciful with them, is poison. And Allah’s established way of tearing down the screen of those who attack the Islamic scholars is well-known. That is because attacking them for an affair that they are innocent of is a mighty thing – and to speak of their honour with falsehood and fabrications is an evil and noxious pasture to graze upon! To concoct falsehood against those whom Allah has chosen to disseminate knowledge is a despicable characteristic. And to emulate those whom Allah has praised; which is the saying of those who followed the believers, that they would seek forgiveness for those who preceded them – that is a noble characteristic. Allah said in His Book, in praise of them: “And those who came after them say, ‘Our Lord! Forgive us and our brethren who have preceded us in Faith, and put not in our hearts any hatred against those who have believed. Our Lord! You are indeed full of kindness, Most Merciful.’” And the one who lets loose his tongue against the Islamic scholars with slander, then Allah will afflict him before his actual death by killing his heart: “And let those who oppose the Messenger’s commandment beware, lest some Fitnah (affliction) befall them or a painful punishment be inflicted on them.” [See Tabyin Kazib Al-Muftarī page 28-30]

Imam At-Tahawi (rahimahullah) stated in his Aqidah:

“And the Islamic scholars of the Salaf, from the early ones and those who came after them from the Tabiʿin: they are the people of goodness, people of narrations (ahlul-Athar), and people of understanding (ahlul-fiqh) and insight – they are not to be mentioned except with fine and beautiful speech. The one who speaks of them with bad speech is not upon the correct path.”

Ash-Shaikh Salih Al-Fawzan (hafizahullah) commented:

“The author moves on from the Sahabah to mention those who come after them in virtue, and they are the Islamic scholars. So the Islamic scholars of this Ummah have status and virtue after the Sahabah because they are the inheritors of the Prophets due to the saying of the Messenger, ‘The scholars are the inheritors of the Prophets’. And the intent here is the Islamic scholars, the people of knowledge, insight and understanding, ahlul-athar, and they are ahlul-Hadīth…”

Abdullah Ibn Mubarak (rahimahullah) said:

“Whoever belittles the Islamic scholars has lost his Hereafter. Whoever belittles the leaders has lost his worldly affairs. Whoever belittles his brothers has lost his honour.” [See Siyaru A’lamin Nubala’, of Imam Az-Zahabī, volume 8, page 408]

Khatib Al-Baghdadī narrated from Shaʿabi who said: Ibn Abbas took hold of the stirrups of the riding beast of Zaid Ibn Thabit (RA). So Zaid said:

“You take hold of them for me whilst you are the son of the uncle of Allah’s Messenger (Peace be upon him)?” Ibn Abbas replied, “Verily this is how we behave with the Islamic scholars.” [See Al-Jami’ li Akhlaq Ar-Rawi wa Adabis-Sami’, volume 1, page 188]

Yahya Ibn Saʿid: Shuʿbah said to me:

“Whosoever I wrote Hadith from, I was with him as a servant.” [Siyaru A’lamin Nubala, volume 7, page 208]

So the Islamic scholars are to be respected and honoured and not belittled, attacked and reviled. The one who belittles them seeks to raise his own status among the masses and to turn them away from Allah’s religion. A Muslim should not be in doubt or ambiguity concerning those who have turned away from the Islamic scholars and turned from the callers to truth and call for a new “understanding” of the religion through their Eurocentric, Modernist, Liberal or Afrocentric lens. The Religion of Allah is one, and the Messenger of Allah (Peace be upon him) left us upon clear proof with respect to it, and upon us is to follow and to remain with those whom the Prophet Muhammad (Peace be upon him) described in the following Hadith:

“There shall not cease to remain a group from my Ummah, steadfast upon the command of Allah. They are not harmed by those who abandon them nor by those who oppose them until the command of Allah comes – and they shall be manifest over the people.” [Reported by Muslim]

Imam Muhammad Ibn Isma’īl Al-Bukharī said: Ali Ibn Al-Madini said:

“They are Ashabul-Hadīth.”

They are the Islamic scholars as the Companion, Muʿawiyah (RA) stated in the first Hadith above.

Imam At-Tirmidhi reported from Ibn Umar that Allah’s Messenger (Peace be upon him) said:

“Allah will not unite my Ummah upon misguidance. And the Hand of Allah is with the Jama’ah, and whoever deviates from that, he deviates himself to the Fire.”

Abu Isa At-Tirmidhī said:

“And the meaning of Al-Jama’ah in the view of the Islamic scholars is: The people of understanding and knowledge and Hadīth.”

So the Jama’ah about whom the Messenger of Allah (Peace be upon him) said: “The Hand of Allah is with the Jama’ah,” are the Islamic scholars and whoever deviates from that Jamaʿah, “deviates himself to the Fire.”

So beware of being drawn into this innovated speech that seeks to belittle the Islamic scholars of our time. And we remind those who fell into this sin with the words of Shaikh Rabī’ (rahimahullah):

“We ask Allah that He guides them to repent, and that they return to the Truth, that they recognise the position of the People of Truth, that they abandon their stance in front of those who are eager for the Truth so they do not prevent them from the Path of Allah.”

Dear brothers and sisters! Now we understand that, the famous saying “the flesh of Islamic scholars is poisoned” (Luhumul-Ulama’ masmumah) is a historic warning by the great classical Islamic scholar, Al-Hafiz, Imam Ali Ibn al-Hasan Ibn Asakir. reminding Muslim believers that disrespecting or backbiting those who carry Prophetic knowledge brings severe spiritual harm and divine retribution.

As mentioned earlier, the classical historian and great Islamic scholar Al-Hafiz, Imam Ibn Asakir, may Allah have mercy on him, famously wrote that the flesh of scholars is poisoned, and whoever lets their tongue attack the honour of the learned will be punished by Allah with the death of their heart before their physical death.

Islamic teachings emphasise that true Islamic scholars do not leave behind gold or silver, but rather knowledge. Honouring them is part of exalting Allah and respecting the message they preserve. Speaking ill of righteous Islamic scholars or making false accusations against them hardens and destroys one’s spiritual connection to Allah.

Allah protects the Islamic scholars, those who truly believe and guide others; attacking their integrity invites humiliation and a ruined hereafter.

Constructive critique based on evidence is different from malicious fault-finding, insults, and tearing down the honour of Ummah guides on social media or public forums.

And understand that the supplication and Du’a of a wronged person carries devastating spiritual weight, and when that person is a man or woman of religious knowledge, an alim or a scholar, wronging them or driving them to pray against you invites swift divine retribution.

Islamic scholars carry the legacy of the Prophets; harming their honour or rights is an assault on truth itself.

Their frequent Zikr, taqwa, and pure reliance make their hearts tender and alert before their Lord.

An Islamic scholar who is genuinely oppressed needs no intermediary; their plea ascends straight to the Throne.

The Prophet Muhammad (Peace be upon him) said:

“Beware of the supplication of the oppressed, for there is no barrier between it and Allah.”

When an authority or a layperson unjustly attacks, mocks, or harms a devoted Islamic scholar, and the Islamic scholar raises their hands in pain, Divine Justice moves immediately to dismantle the oppressor’s peace, wealth, or standing.

Countless historical accounts warn that leaders and common folk who ruined the dignity of righteous Islamic scholars found their own lives collapsing in sudden ruin.

Believing a scholar’s piety prevents them from crying out to Allah is a dangerous delusion; desperation strips away formal patience, leaving raw, piercing sincerity.

Finally, on the other hand, to maintain their dignity and to protect their integrity and noble position, Islam strictly prohibits Islamic scholars, Ulama, from participating in, endorsing, assisting or supporting any form of injustice against the poor citizens. Islamic scholars are bound by divine command to speak the truth, guide society toward equity, and actively refuse cooperation with the oppressors.

Allah Almighty states in a sacred tradition (Hadith Qudsi) that:

“O My servants, I have forbidden injustice for Myself and have made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another.”

Islamic scholars inherit the mantle of the Prophets and Messengers of Allah, making the defense of justice an absolute religious duty rather than an optional choice.

Prophetic traditions warn that those Islamic scholars who validate a leader’s falsehoods or assist in their oppression dissociate themselves from the Prophet’s guidance.

Authentic Islamic scholarship requires confronting wrongdoing directly and advising leaders with love, justice and wisdom.

Assisting an unjust system — even through minor acts or silent endorsement — violates the Qur’anic injunction:

“And do not cooperate in sin and injustice.”

Islamic scholars are obligated to defend victims of tyranny regardless of religion, region, status, ethnicity, or background.

So our great religion (Islam) strictly prohibits Islamic scholars from participating in, endorsing, assisting or supporting any form of injustice. Islamic scholars carry a heavy religious duty to uphold the truth, speak against tyranny, and guide society with integrity.

The following is the Arabic text of Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir words:

All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may the salutations of peace, security and blessings be upon our beloved Prophet Muhammad, upon his family, upon all his Companions and true followers.

Murtadha Muhammad Gusau is the Chief Imam of Nagazi-Uvete Jumu’ah and the late Alhaji Abdur-Rahman Okene’s Mosques, Okene, Kogi State, Nigeria. He can be reached via: [email protected] or +2348038289761 or +2348024192217.
